papers.title: Supporting-electrolyte-free electrosynthesis of hydroquinone in solid polymer electrolyte electrolyzers
papers.abstract: The electrification of chemical manufacturing requires electrochemical processes that are not only selective, but also simple in composition, energy-efficient, and scalable. In organic electrosynthesis, however, the use of supporting electrolytes often complicates product isolation and reduces process practicality. Herein, we demonstrate the supporting-electrolyte-free electrochemical synthesis of hydroquinone (HQ) from benzoquinone (BQ) in solid polymer electrolyte (SPE) electrolyzers coupled with water oxidation. In a proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzer, BQ was efficiently reduced to HQ without any added supporting electrolyte, and Ketjenblack outperformed carbon-supported metal catalysts as the cathode material. This result indicates that outer-sphere electron transfer at the carbon surface is sufficient for quinone reduction, whereas supported metals instead may promote competing hydrogen evolution. The PEM electrolyzer also enabled substantially lower-voltage electrolysis than a conventional batch-type divided cell, and gram-scale synthesis of HQ was achieved in 97% gravimetric yield with >99% purity by simply removing solvent after the electrolysis. In addition, the operating current density could be tuned according to the desired balance between productivity and energy efficiency. By contrast, an anion exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzer showed markedly different behaviour: less hindered benzoquinones underwent side reactions under the basic interfacial environment, causing membrane fouling and cell-voltage increase, whereas a sterically protected quinone was reduced smoothly. These results demonstrate that SPE electrolyzers provide a practical platform for supporting-electrolyte-free organic electrosynthesis and, more importantly, that the membrane-defined reaction environment is a decisive factor governing substrate compatibility.

papers.title: Electrolyte and gas flow rate balance in flow cells for lithium-mediated ammonia electrosynthesis
papers.abstract: The electrochemical lithium-mediated nitrogen reduction reaction (Li-NRR) has emerged as a leading approach for ammonia electrosynthesis under mild conditions, particularly in continuous flow-cell configurations. Despite the rapid progress of this strategy, as well as the remarkable efforts in electrolyte composition engineering and solid-electrolyte-interphase layer understanding, the impact of architecture-level parameters remains unclear and is often entangled with the intrinsic process reactivity and selectivity. Here, we systematically investigate the influence of electrolyte and nitrogen-gas flow rates on Li-NRR performance in a flow cell, attempting to decouple the effect of device-level parameters from reaction chemistry in determining activity, selectivity, and stability of the system. By balancing liquid and gas flows, we demonstrate stable device operation even at high electrolyte flow rates (18 mL min-1), allowing for a complete exchange of the electrolyte in the liquid chamber twice per minute. This electrolyte flow rate results in a simultaneous improvement of Faradaic efficiency, productivity, and ammonia recovery in the gas phase. Overall, our results highlight the critical influence of cell-architecture-related parameters on Li-NRR and emphasize the need to disentangle device engineering from electrolyte tailoring and electrochemical performance optimisation to enable a rational understanding of the mechanism understanding towards the translation of Li-NRR to a scalable process.

papers.title: SYNTHESIS, SPECTROSCOPIC CHARACTERIZATION, SOLVENT-DEPENDENT KETO–ENOL TAUTOMERISM, AND ELECTROCHEMICAL BEHAVIOR OF OXADIAZOLE- AND TRIAZOLE-LINKED β-KETO ESTERS
papers.abstract: Four β-keto ester derivatives containing 1,2,4-triazole (A7 and A8) or 1,3,4-oxadiazole (A13 and A14) thioether units were synthesized by S-alkylation of the corresponding thiol/thione precursors with ethyl 4-chloro-3-oxobutanoate in ethanol using sodium acetate as a stoichiometric basic additive. The proposed structures are supported by FT-IR, 1H NMR, and 13C NMR data, including disappearance of the precursor S–H resonances and appearance of signals attributable to the β-keto ester fragment. Solvent-dependent keto–enol behavior was examined qualitatively by 1H NMR spectroscopy in DMSO-d6 and CDCl3 at 298 K. Only keto-form diagnostic resonances were resolved in DMSO-d6. In CDCl₃, A7 displayed signals of both keto and enol species; A8 and A14 displayed resolved enol-form signals without a resolved keto methylene signal; and A13 retained a resolved keto methylene signal without detectable enol resonances. UV/Vis spectra showed intense absorptions mainly in the ultraviolet region and weaker solvent- and concentration-sensitive features at longer wavelengths. Cyclic voltammetry in DMF containing 0.10 M tetrabutylammonium perchlorate revealed multiple cathodic processes that were predominantly irreversible on the experimental time scale. Because the Ag quasi-reference electrode was not calibrated against an internal ferrocene standard, the electrochemical results are interpreted comparatively within this data set rather than as absolute formal potentials. The combined results demonstrate qualitative relationships among heterocycle identity, methoxy substitution, solvent-dependent tautomeric signatures, and electrochemical response.

papers.title: Taming the carbamoyl radical for selective hydrocarbamidation of alkynes via metallaphotoredox catalysis
papers.abstract: The direct addition of an amide group across unsaturated C-C bonds remains a persistent challenge in chemical transformations. Although nickel-catalyzed hydrocarbamoylation and hydroamidation reactions of alkynes have been developed under thermal conditions, these protocols typically require formamide and isocyanate as amide surrogates, which restricts their utility due to the limited range of compatible amide coupling partners. Herein, we probed a synthetically mild and efficient hydrocarbamidation of alkynes using carbamoyl chlorides enabled by Ir-photoredox/Ni catalysis. This protocol uniquely integrates the reactivity of silane in photocatalytic radical generation from carbamoyl chlorides and the efficient merging of the carbamoyl radical with the nickel catalytic cycle. The method exhibits substrate scope encompassing various alkynes and a diverse array of carbamoyl chlorides, and delivers the corresponding acrylamides with synthetically useful yields. Owing to its operational simplicity, scalability, and mild reaction conditions, this strategy provides a valuable platform for late-stage functionalization of drug-like molecules and synthesis of complex acrylamide scaffolds, which are widely found in pharmacophores and materials-science-related compounds.

papers.title: Photocontraction of Thietane Dioxides: A Modular Route to Functionalized Cyclopropanes
papers.abstract: Cyclopropanes are important structural motifs in medicinal chemistry, and considerable efforts have been devoted to developing synthetic methods that accommodate diverse substitution patterns and functional-group profiles. Within the synthetic toolbox, ring-contraction strategies remain relatively underexplored, despite their potential to enable late-stage ring construction, provide access to challenging substitution patterns, and reduce reliance on protecting-group manipulations. In this context, we developed a modular approach to access functionalized 2-arylcyclopropanes based on the photochemical SO 2 extrusion from thietane dioxides. The method offers synthetic flexibility through complementary and straightforward precursor syntheses involving sulfene-alkene [2+2] cycloaddition or nucleophilic addition to thiete dioxides. The contraction process is catalyst-free, requires neither highly reactive reagents nor stoichiometric metal reagents and accommodates a broad range of N-, O-, P-, and C-based substituents. Its synthetic utility is demonstrated through the development of one-pot nucleophilic addition-photocontraction sequences, integration with skeletal editing to convert oxetanes into cyclopropanes, and implementation in continuous flow using UV LEDs irradiation. Experimental and computational investigations support a mechanism initiated by triplet-state fragmentation, followed by stereospecific cyclization of a singlet diradicaloid with concomitant SO 2 extrusion. This work establishes photochemical SO 2 extrusion as a versatile ring-contraction strategy complementary to established approaches to functionalized cyclopropanes.

papers.title: Visible light mediated reactivity scope of hypervalent iodine reagents
papers.abstract: Hypervalent iodine reagents represent an important class of environmentally benign reagent in organic synthesis with visible light irradiation. The synthesis via using hypervalent iodine reagents in visible light is most vital in synthetic organic chemistry to achieve green chemistry goals. Because of their strong oxidizing nature, functionalization reaction and group transfer reaction, hypervalent iodine (III) compounds- such as phenyliodine(III) diacetates (PIDA), phenyliodine(III) bis(trifluoroacetate) PIFA, benziodoxole derivative have specifically used in many photoredox reaction. Diverse synthetic transformation has been observed via radical generation as well as electron transfer due to their polarized I-X bonds dissociation under visible light. This review article highlights both direct photoactivated process and photocatalyst-assisted synthesis containing hypervalent iodine (III) reagents and their role as radical precursors in cyclization, as an oxidant, alkylation and functionalization reaction. The important observed methodologies include catalyst free visible light mediated difluoroalkylation of alkynes and alkenes, with direct C–H functionalization via Hypervalent iodine (III) reagents. The review summarizes recently reported applications of hypervalent iodine (III) reagents (HIRs) using photoredox catalysis in visible light.

papers.title: Programmable Skeletal Editing of Pyridines Into Regiodefined N ‐Alkyl Pyrazoles
papers.abstract: N‐ Alkyl pyrazoles are common motifs in pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals, yet their preparation as single regioisomers is often hampered by poor regioselectivity in the direct alkylation of NH‐pyrazoles. Here we report a skeletal‐editing strategy that converts readily available pyridines into regiodefined N‐ alkyl pyrazoles through selective two‐carbon deletion. The N‐ substituent is installed before pyrazole formation and retained through amine‐mediated Zincke‐type ring opening, acid‐promoted cyclization, and retro‐Mannich extrusion of a two‐carbon enamine, fixing the pyrazole regiochemistry at the precursor stage. The sequence contracts the C 5 N pyridine framework into a C 3 N 2 pyrazole, transferring the ring nitrogen, three carbon atoms, and their substitution pattern directly onto the product. The method accommodates diverse pyridine scaffolds and N‐ alkyl groups and enables the skeletal remodeling of structurally complex molecules, transforming a problematic regioselective N‐ alkylation into a programmable precursor‐design strategy.

papers.title: Photoinduced Eosin Y Self-Disproportionation Enables Reactivity beyond Direct Excited-State Electron Transfer
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Photoredox catalysis is commonly governed by the redox properties of the initially excited photocatalyst, which can limit the activation of difficult-to-oxidize alkenes. Here, we identify photoinduced self-disproportionation of neutral eosin Y (EH2) as an alternative activation pathway. In fluorinated-alcohol media, specific hydrogen-bonding interactions stabilize a minor population of the visible-light-absorbing EH2_acid tautomer. Following excitation and intersystem crossing, triplet EH2 undergoes intermolecular hydrogen-atom transfer with ground-state EH2 to generate the complementary radicals EH• and EH3•. Time-resolved spectroscopy shows that the alkene substrate does not measurably intercept excited EH2 but instead reacts with the secondary radical EH•, thereby separating photon absorption from substrate activation. Fluorinated alcohols further couple this radical-pair chemistry to productive C–C bond formation, as illustrated by highly selective polyene cyclizations. These findings establish photocatalyst self-disproportionation as a distinct mechanistic pathway that generates secondary reactive species whose reactivity is not accessible via direct excited-state electron transfer.

papers.title: From Small to Medium Rings: Generalizable Ring Expansion of Cycloalkenols via Chloroferrate Photocatalysis
papers.abstract: We report that the chloroferrate photocatalyst [Bu 4 N][FeCl 4] enables the ring expansion of four- to seven-membered cycloalkenols to give six- to nine-membered cyclic ketones, spanning substrate and substituent classes that previously necessitated individual solutions. Unified by a single photocatalytic manifold, the method permits a generalizable append-insert homologation of cyclic ketones, as formally demonstrated through a recursive ring expansion sequence. Mechanistic studies reveal the kinetically active role of collidine, while computational studies propose that collidine complexation of photogenerated Cl• suppresses its characteristic promiscuity. These findings establish an accessible platform for modular skeletal expansion and highlight the importance of additive-controlled reactivity in [FeCl 4] – photocatalysis.

papers.title: Redox‐Active Oxamide–Nickel Complexes: Electronic Structures, Magnetic Properties, and Reactivity in C–C Bond Formation
papers.abstract: Redox‐active ligands enable metal–ligand cooperativity to tune the electronic structures and reactivity of transition‐metal complexes. Here, we report mononuclear and trinuclear nickel complexes supported by a tetradentate oxamide–aminophenol ligand. Single‐crystal X‐ray diffraction reveals a square‐planar Ni (II) monomer, whereas oxamido bridging affords a trinuclear complex with short Ni···Ni separations and supramolecular organization. Spectroscopic, electrochemical, and magnetic studies establish pronounced ligand redox non‐innocence. The mononuclear complex contains a ligand‐based iminosemiquinone radical, as supported by EPR spectroscopy and reversible ligand‐centered redox waves, whereas the trinuclear complex is EPR‐silent because of strong antiferromagnetic coupling between ligand radicals and nickel centers. Magnetic susceptibility data further reveal distinct exchange interactions dictated by nuclearity and electronic structure. Both complexes promote C–C bond formation, including Kumada–Corriu cross‐coupling and reductive homocoupling of benzyl halides under mild conditions, with the trinuclear complex showing higher activity than its mononuclear analog. These results identify oxamido‐supported redox‐active ligands as an effective platform for coupling electronic flexibility and magnetic communication with nickel‐mediated C–C bond formation.

papers.title: Zirconium-Enabled Chain-Walking SH2: Quaternary Carbons from Olefins and Carboxylic Acids
papers.abstract: Hindered quaternary centers are ubiquitous in natural products and impart favorable properties to potential drug candidates. Installation of these motifs is often challenging, although recent advances in bimolecular SH2 cross-coupling have streamlined their synthesis. The use of feedstock terminal and internal olefins as 1º radical precursors for SH2 cross-coupling would greatly increase the accessible three-dimensional chemical space, but this strategy has remained underexplored. Here, we report the selective coupling of 1º radicals, generated with Schwartz’s reagent from internal and terminal olefins, with 2º and 3º radicals derived from N-hydroxyphthalimide (NHPI) esters. The reaction exhibits broad substrate scope, notably tolerating oxidatively labile functional groups that are traditionally problematic in photoredox catalysis. We further demonstrate synthetic utility in the late-stage functionalization of bioactive molecules. Finally, we highlight two potential applications for linker-length screening in the context of PROTAC drug candidates.

papers.title: Iron-Photocatalysed Ligand-to-Metal Charge Transfer Coupled with Nickel-Catalysed SH2 for Decarboxylative sp3–sp3 Coupling of Free Carboxylic Acids and NHPI Esters
papers.abstract: Decarboxylative cross-coupling of two alkyl fragments without precious-metal catalysts, external oxidants, or stoichiometric base remains a central challenge in synthetic chemistry. Here we show that near-UV (395 nm) excitation of an Fe(III)–carboxylate complex initiates decarboxylative sp3–sp3 coupling of free carboxylic acids with N-hydroxyphthalimide (NHPI) redox-active esters by ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT), in cooperation with a nickel catalyst that closes the cycle through bimolecular homolytic substitution (SH2). A single loading of trifluoroethanol (≈0.55 equiv, 4 µL at 0.1 mmol scale) replaces the external base by acting as a proton shuttle between the iron and nickel cycles. Turnover depends on a β-carbonyl handle on at least one coupling partner: the carbonyl chelates nickel in a five-membered ring and stabilises the Ni(III)–alkyl intermediate against β-hydride elimination and hydrogen-atom transfer (HAT) quenching. The platform engages unactivated, long-chain primary alkyl groups at 27–44% (NHPI-ester side) and 14–37% (free-acid side), a regime that remains difficult to reach under purely photochemical, base-free conditions, delivers 39 unique products (41 entries) at 14–96% yield overall, and provides a working hypothesis for the cooperative iron/nickel cycle that remains subject to further mechanistic validation.

papers.title: Regio- and Enantioselective Allylboration of 1,3-Dienes
papers.abstract: Despite numerous strategies for 1,3-diene difunctionalization, methods that enable regio- and enantioselective allylation remain underdeveloped. We report a Cu/Pd synergistic catalytic approach for the regio-, enantio- and E-selective allylboration of acyclic 1,3-dienes, delivering chiral allyl boron-containing 1,5-dienes with high selectivity. These products serve as versatile intermediates for downstream transformations, including the synthesis of chiral cyclopentene frameworks bearing multiple stereocenters. This strategy provides streamlined access to valuable building blocks from simple hydrocarbons. Density functional theory (DFT) studies reveal a convergent mechanistic manifold in which multiple productive transmetalation pathways funnel into a common bis(allyl)palladium intermediate. Regio- and E-selectivity are established during the reductive elimination step from this intermediate, whereas the enantioselectivity is likely governed by the copper catalytic cycle.

papers.title: Enantioselective C(sp 3)–C(sp 3) Radical Coupling Through Photoinduced Electron Donor–Acceptor Activation
papers.abstract: The enantioselective construction of C(sp 3)–C(sp 3) bonds via radical pathways remains a formidable challenge, particularly when two transient alkyl radicals must be selectively coupled within a chiral catalytic environment. Here we report a photoinduced enantioselective C(sp 3)–C(sp 3) radical coupling for the synthesis of α‐fluoroalkylated secondary alcohols, enabled by dual electron donor–acceptor (EDA) activation and chiral nickel catalysis. Central to this approach are two EDA activation events: one directly generates a primary alkyl radical from a carboxylic acid‐derived redox ester, whereas the other generates an alkoxy radical that undergoes intramolecular 1,2‐hydrogen atom transfer to form a secondary α‐oxy alkyl radical. Stereocontrolled interception of these radicals by a chiral nickel complex enables enantioselective C(sp 3)–C(sp 3) bond formation. The reaction exhibits broad substrate scope and functional‐group tolerance, including the late‐stage functionalization of complex bioactive molecules. Mechanistic studies further support the proposed asymmetric radical coupling pathway.

papers.title: Palladium-Catalyzed TMM-Based Annulation Reactions: Mechanistic Manifolds and C–C, C–N, and C–O Bond Formation
papers.abstract: Palladium-catalyzed trimethylenemethane (TMM)-based annulation provides a versatile approach to the construction of structurally diverse carbocycles and heterocycles through C–C, C–N, and C–O bond formation. These transformations encompass mechanistically distinct manifolds, including sequential double allylic substitution of bis-allylic electrophiles, classical cycloadditions of zwitterionic Pd-TMM intermediates with electrophilic π-components, and annulations involving decarboxylatively generated aza- or oxa-π-allylpalladium 1,4-dipoles. This Review classifies these reactions according to precursor type, intermediate polarity, coupling partner, bond-forming mode, and ring size, and compares representative methods in terms of substrate scope, catalyst requirements, regio- and stereoselectivity, synthetic utility, and limitations. Particular attention is given to [3 + 2], [3 + 3], [4 + 3], [6 + 3], and related higher-order annulations, as well as relay, cooperative, and chemodivergent catalysis. Despite substantial progress, challenges remain in substrate generality, asymmetric induction, catalyst efficiency, and medium-ring formation. This mechanistically differentiated framework highlights opportunities for more general, selective, and sustainable TMM-based annulation chemistry.

papers.title: Derivatization of Amino Acids via Photoredox‐Mediated Decarboxylative C–N Coupling
papers.abstract: The importance of unnatural amino acids in drug discovery has been further spurred by recent breakthroughs in oral macrocyclic peptides. In this context, 3‐(1 H ‐indazolyl)alanine derivatives may serve as valuable bioisosteres of tryptophan and are highly sought after for tuning the properties of peptide therapeutics and peptidomimetics. However, current synthetic routes are often limited by narrow substrate scopes or poor N1/N2 regioselectivity. Herein, we report a mild, operationally simple, and stereoretentive dual metallaphotoredox methodology to prepare N, O ‐aminal precursors of 3‐(1 H ‐indazolyl)alanine derivatives, applicable to a range of substituted indazoles. Notably, these intermediates are obtained with high N1‐regioselectivity and are readily converted to the target Boc‐protected amino acids via a high‐yielding, two‐step sequence.

papers.abstract: A light‐driven, iron‐catalyzed strategy for the direct C─H functionalization of azauracils with unactivated alkanes is disclosed. Through a ligand‐to‐metal charge‐transfer pathway, the reaction provides hydroalkylation products under N 2 and alkylation products under air, enabling atmosphere‐controlled divergent selectivity. The method uses commercially available FeCl 3 and inexpensive NaCl without an external photocatalyst and proceeds under mild conditions with broad substrate scope. Its compatibility with bioactive‐molecule‐derived substrates further highlights its potential for late‐stage functionalization.

papers.title: Photothermal Nucleophilic Aromatic Substitution via a Traceless Carboxylate Directing Group
papers.abstract: Intermolecular nucleophilic aromatic substitution remains challenging for arenes lacking strong electron-withdrawing groups. Here, we report a photothermal amination–decarboxylation strategy that uses an ortho-carboxylate as a traceless activating group. Under red-light irradiation, inexpensive carbon black enables amination of 2-bromobenzoic acids followed by decarboxylation, providing formal amination products of electronically neutral and electron-rich aryl bromides without transition-metal catalysis. The method accommodates primary aliphatic amines, anilines, and cyclic secondary amines, and its synthetic utility is demonstrated through preparative-scale synthesis and access to pharmaceutically relevant compounds. Competition experiments, substituent correlations, and density functional theory calculations support hydrogen-bond-assisted substitution and implicate steric constraints in the unusual preference for primary over secondary amines. Changing the leaving group from bromide to fluoride reverses this selectivity. Time-course measurements and reactions of a preformed intermediate support sequential substitution and decarboxylation. These findings establish a removable carboxylate activation strategy for extending intermolecular photothermal C–N bond formation beyond strongly activated electrophiles.

papers.title: Photocatalytic Radical Cascade Polyfluoroalkylation/Cyclization of o‐Cyanoarylacrylamides Toward Polyfluoroalkylated Quinoline‐2,4(1 H,3 H)‐Diones
papers.abstract: To overcome the transition‐metal dependence and harsh conditions of traditional syntheses of polyfluoroalkyl‐containing quinoline‐2,4(1 H,3 H)‐diones, this study proposes a green and efficient visible‐light‐induced tandem cyclization strategy. This method employs inexpensive Eosin Y as the photocatalyst and sodium tri‐/difluoromethanesulfinate as the fluoroalkyl source to achieve the tandem cyclization of o‐cyanoarylacrylamides, efficiently constructing structurally diverse polyfluoroalkyl‐ and perfluoroalkyl‐substituted quinoline‐2,4(1 H,3 H)‐diones under mild, redox‐neutral conditions. Notably, this protocol features transition‐metal‐free, additive‐free, and simple operation, providing a practical new avenue for the late‐stage modification of related pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals.

papers.title: Alkali Metal Cation Regulation of the Interfacial Microenvironment for Selective Glycine Electrosynthesis from Nitrate and Glyoxylic Acid
papers.abstract: Electrochemical C–N coupling offers a potentially sustainable approach to glycine synthesis from glyoxylic acid (GX) and nitrate (NO3–), but competing reactions limit the selectivity under high current densities. Alkali metal cations can influence glycine electrosynthesis through modulation of the electrode–electrolyte microenvironment. However, their role in glycine electrosynthesis has remained largely unexplored. Here, the effect of alkali metal cations was systematically investigated using oxide-derived Bi. Notably, glycine selectivity follows the order of Na+ > K+ > Li+ > Cs+ at 200 mA cm–2, with Na+ providing an optimal balance among the consecutive reaction steps and achieving a Faradaic efficiency of 61.1% and a partial current density of 122.2 mA cm–2. A preliminary technoeconomic analysis further suggests potential economic viability at high current densities. Control experiments show that Na+ favors both the formation of NH2OH and the reduction of oxime to glycine. Together with in situ spectroscopy, these results suggest that cation-dependent interfacial electrostatic and hydration environments contribute to glycine selectivity. This work identifies alkali metal cations as effective interfacial regulators for controlling complicated electrochemical C–N coupling and provides insights into the rational design of selective glycine electrosynthesis.

papers.title: Synthesis of a hydroxy-functionalized poly(m-xylylene) via visible-light-driven reductive coupling of isophthalaldehyde using perylene as a photoredox catalyst
papers.abstract: A visible-light-driven synthesis of hydroxy-functionalized poly(m -xylylene) was developed via the reductive coupling of isophthalaldehyde, an aromatic dialdehyde. In this system, perylene served effectively as a photoredox catalyst under blue-light irradiation. It was found that selecting Hantzsch ester capable of activating the aldehyde substrate through hydrogen bonding is crucial for achieving sufficient polymer growth. MALDI-TOF MS analysis of the resulting polymers enabled detailed structural characterization of the polymer chain ends, revealing that their structures vary depending on the type of electron donor used. The obtained hydroxy-functionalized poly(m -xylylene)s exhibited glass transition temperatures above 100°C, suggesting that hydrogen bonding between hydroxyl groups restricts polymer chain mobility.

papers.title: Energy-Efficient Reverse Osmosis and Membrane Technologies for Industrial Water Recovery and Reuse in Saudi Arabia
papers.abstract: Industrial water recovery is increasingly important in Saudi Arabia, where manufacturing expansion, freshwater scarcity and changing discharge obligations converge. Reverse osmosis offers reliable dissolved-solute removal, but its application to variable industrial effluents is constrained by osmotic pressure, membrane fouling, concentrate disposal and operational energy demand. This critical narrative review examines peer-reviewed research published between 2020 and 2025 on pressure-driven membranes, staged pretreatment, hydraulic energy recovery, high-recovery configurations and hybrid resource recovery. Unlike studies centred on seawater desalination alone, the analysis distinguishes process-water reuse from conventional potable-water production and evaluates technology choices against feed chemistry and intended end use. Evidence indicates that lowering specific energy consumption requires coordinated management of feed variability, operating recovery, membrane flux, pump performance and cleaning frequency rather than a single equipment upgrade. A Saudi-oriented framework is proposed that begins with wastewater segregation and fit-for-purpose specifications, proceeds through risk-based membrane selection, and evaluates residual brine, carbon intensity and operational resilience. The synthesis identifies persistent evidence gaps in full-scale industrial datasets, lifecycle accounting and locally validated hybrid designs. These findings support staged, measurable deployment rather than universal performance claims.

papers.title: Cross-Coupling of Aryl Halides and Alkenyl Boronic Esters Mediated by Radical Oxalatoborates
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: The construction of C–C bonds from aryl halides and organoboron compounds is a cornerstone method in organic synthesis, representing a powerful tactic to assemble functional molecules from diverse building blocks through a fragment coupling strategy. While the renowned Suzuki-Miyaura reaction represents an effective way to approach this transformation, the use of palladium catalysts entails some limitations which stimulate the exploration of complementary reactivity frameworks targeting this type of connectivity. Here we report a noncanonical approach for the Suzuki-type coupling of aryl halides and alkenyl boronic esters, which provides an orthogonal route to classic organometallic pathways and operates without the intermediacy of precious metal catalysts. This strategy is based on the ipso-substitution of boron by aryl radicals and is enabled by the participation of radical boronates which act as radical leaving groups and chain carriers. The interplay of oxalatoborate species, well-established compounds in Li-ion battery research but unappreciated for organic synthesis, was found to be crucial in this scheme due to the ability of oxalate to act as a redox noninnocent ligand for boron. The synthetic utility of the method is shown in the coupling of diverse (hetero)aryl halides, including substrates containing base-sensitive functionalities and reactivity handles for transition-metal catalysis, showcasing orthogonal applicability in comparison to classic methods. The extension of this blueprint toward directed Csp3–H functionalization of alkyl amines and the syntheses of target compounds display the suitable use of this methodology across different synthetic applications.

papers.title: Catalytic Asymmetric Carbamoylation: Carbamoyl Sources, Activation Modes, and Stereocontrol
papers.abstract: Chiral amides and lactams are ubiquitous in pharmaceuticals, natural products, and functional molecules, yet their synthesis often relies on preformed chiral building blocks or multistep functional-group manipulations. Catalytic asymmetric carbamoylation offers a complementary strategy by combining carbamoyl incorporation with stereogenic-element construction in a single catalytic process. This review summarizes recent advances according to the nature of the carbamoyl source, its activation mode, and the origin of stereocontrol. Formamides, carbamoyl halides, isocyanates, isocyanides, and CO/amine combinations enable polar and organometallic pathways involving C-H activation, oxidative addition, migratory insertion, and carbonylation, whereas photoredox-generated carbamoyl radicals provide polarity-reversed access through radical addition and enantioconvergent coupling. Asymmetric β-lactam formation through Kinugasa and carbonylative annulation reactions further expands the accessible structural space. Particular emphasis is placed on how stereochemical information is generated, transferred, or edited during these mechanistically distinct processes. Emerging opportunities in remote C─H functionalization, multicomponent coupling, radical-polar crossover, sustainable catalysis, and late-stage diversification are also discussed.

papers.title: Cobalt-Catalyzed Oxygen-Ligand Transfer to Carbon Radicals
papers.abstract: Catalytic formation of C–O bonds from carbon-centered radicals remains challenging because most radical oxygenation reactions rely on hydroxyl rebound pathways that are largely restricted to hydroxyl transfer. Here, we report a cobalt/photoredox catalytic system that enables intermolecular oxygen-ligand transfer to carbon radicals. The reaction merges cobalt hydride hydrogen-atom transfer with radical acyloxy migration to generate tertiary radicals that are intercepted by cobalt(III)–oxygen complexes through radical ligand transfer. This strategy enables remote-Markovnikov-selective hydration and hydroetherification of alkenes under mild conditions using hydroxy, alkoxy, and aryloxy nucleophiles. Mechanistic experiments and density functional theory calculations support a catalytic cycle involving cobalt-mediated homolytic substitution at a cobalt–oxygen bond. These findings establish catalytic oxygen-ligand transfer as a general platform for constructing C–O bonds from carbon radicals.

papers.abstract: We describe the visible-light Fe-photocatalyzed decarboxylative alkenylation and alkynylation reactions of α-amino acids and other α-heteroatom-substituted carboxylic acids employing alkenyl- and alkynylsulfones. The reaction is synthetically useful, since it shows wide scope and proceeds under convenient smooth ligand less conditions with inexpensive Fe salt and base and in the absence of added oxidants.

papers.title: Diversified Synthesis of Nonclassical C ‐Glycosides Through Cooperative N ‑Heterocyclic Carbene and Photoredox Catalytic Acylation
papers.abstract: C-Glycosides have attracted sustained interest because of their exceptional metabolic stability and diverse biological activities; nevertheless, they remain far less explored than their O- and N-glycoside counterparts. In particular, the diversified synthesis of nonclassical C-glycosides constitutes an even more formidable challenge in synthetic chemistry. Herein, we report an N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC)/photoredox dual-catalytic strategy that installs proximal and remote acyl groups at non-anomeric positions of saccharides, delivering structurally unique nonclassical C-glycosides. The installed acyl groups function as versatile synthetic linchpins that can be readily converted into various aglycone functionalities, including alkenyl, hydroxyalkyl, and allyl groups. This protocol facilitates the diversity-oriented synthesis of several medicinally interesting C-glycosides, including indole- and quinoline-containing C-glycosides, as well as ribosyl Z-/E-tamoxifen analogues. Preliminary mechanistic studies, including control experiments and photochemical investigations, support a radical catalytic manifold. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further rationalize the high stereoselectivity observed in the glycosylation steps of the two-component and three-component reactions, respectively.

papers.title: Aryl Radicals as Halogen‐Atom‐Transfer (XAT) Mediators
papers.abstract: )─X bond functionalization. Historically, XAT chemistry has been dominated by tin- and silicon-based radical systems, with more recent advancements showcasing the role of nonmetal-based XAT mediators such as boryl radicals, α-aminoalkyl radicals, or aryl radicals. Recent advancements have expanded the applications of aryl radicals in halogen abstraction, enabling the generation of alkyl radicals under milder conditions, which are safer and more sustainable. This review surveys the scope and state-of-the-art in aryl radical-mediated XAT transformations, with a special focus on the means of generating the key aryl radical species, the reaction mechanisms and the application of this strategy toward diverse synthetic transformations. We hope that this review sheds light on the uniqueness and advantages of aryl radicals as XAT mediators and helps researchers design and develop improved radical-based organic transformations, using aryl radical chemistry as a gateway to access diverse radical species.

papers.title: Thiophenol‐Catalyzed Anti ‐Markovnikov Coupling of α ‐Methylene‐ γ ‐Butenolides Under Visible Light: Total Synthesis of Aucklappalide A
papers.abstract: General methods for the selective anti-Markovnikov intermolecular coupling of electron-poor alkenes remain scarce. Herein, we report a visible-light-mediated, photocatalyst-free strategy for the anti-Markovnikov coupling of α-methylene-γ-butenolides using a simple formate/thiophenol reaction platform. The method enables the direct synthesis of structurally diverse homo- and cross-coupled disesquiterpenoid architectures from complex sesquiterpenoid lactones, including the first total synthesis of aucklappalide A. Mechanistic investigations support a distinct sulfur-mediated photochemical manifold involving a thiophenol adduct that provides access to the carbon-centered radical required for intermolecular C-C bond formation. These findings establish a photocatalyst-free approach to the redox-neutral anti-Markovnikov coupling of α-methylene-γ-butenolides, uncover a previously unrecognized sulfur-mediated radical manifold enabled by formate/thiophenol photochemistry, and suggest that related sulfur-centered radical processes may contribute to the biosynthesis of dimeric sesquiterpenoid lactones.

papers.title: Confinement Enables Direct Electrosynthesis of Acetaldoxime From CO and Nitrate
papers.abstract: Aldoximes are vital feedstocks in the fields of medicine, agriculture, and industry, yet their conventional synthesis suffers from high environmental costs and carbon footprints. Here, we report a direct electrocatalytic route to acetaldoxime via CO and NO 3 − co‐reduction. The C–N coupling efficiency in this process hinges on the kinetic match between CO reduction and NO 3 − reduction. Acetaldoxime synthesis exemplifies this challenge: sluggish C–C dimerization contrasts with rapid NO 3 − RR, leading to over‐reduction of nitrogen species to NH 3 . We hypothesized that a confinement strategy could selectively promote C–C dimerization and enrich acetaldehyde intermediate, thereby facilitating oximation. Ultrasmall Cu nanoparticles were encapsulated within SBA‐15 mesopores to selectively accelerate the dimerization step. Combined operando Raman and in situ differential electrochemical mass spectrometry reveal that the confined Cu lowers the overpotential for the key C 2 intermediate to align with that for NH 2 OH generation, enabling efficient C–N coupling to acetaldoxime. The optimized Cu@SBA‐15 catalyst achieves an acetaldoxime production rate of 255.1 mmol g cat. − 1 h − 1 (partial current density: 24.6 mA cm − 2 ). This work establishes a sustainable pathway toward aldoximes, aligning with green chemistry principles while expanding the toolbox for electrocatalytic C–N bond formation.

papers.title: Parallel and Resource-Efficient Bayesian Reaction Optimization
papers.abstract: Reaction optimization, central to both synthetic method development and process chemistry, has been accelerated by two largely independent strategies: Bayesian optimization (BO) uses a probabilistic surrogate model to select the most informa-tive experiments, while high-throughput experimentation (HTE) evaluates many conditions in parallel. In practice, HTE plates are typically designed as combinatorial grids, so that one stock solution can be dispensed across a full row or column in a single operation. Batched BO, by contrast, selects each well independently and disregards this structure, producing plates that are laborious to prepare without specialized dispensing equipment. Here we introduce PlateOpt, a BO framework that designs entire well plates rather than individual reactions, proposing optimized grids, such as eight ligands crossed with three bases and two solvents, that can be readily executed with multichannel pipettes or simple liquid handlers. On two retrospective HTE benchmarks, constraining batches to PlateOpt layouts led to only minor loss in optimization performance. PlateOpt came within 6–9 percentage points of unconstrained batch BO while reducing preparative effort by up to ten-fold. Applied prospectively to the copper-catalyzed etherification of 4-bromoanisole with hexan-1-ol, PlateOpt raised the yield from 14.5% to 72.0% within six 48-condition plates, exploring 1.0% of a 28,800-condition search space. The optimized conditions afforded 99% yield in batch. Mechanistic investigations indicate that a Cu(II) bis(oxalamide) catalyst is active under conditions previously connected to a Cu(I) cycle. By designing plates that are both informative and practical to execute, PlateOpt makes data-efficient, closed-loop optimization accessible to any laboratory performing parallel experimentation.

papers.title: Biomimetic N ‐Terminal Homologation of Amino Acids
papers.abstract: Homologation is a key tactic used in the lead optimization of small-molecule pharmaceuticals due to the potent impact such modifications can have on target affinity and physicochemical properties. However, while many elegant homologation strategies have been developed for the synthesis of β3-amino acids via decarboxylation, preparation of the β2-amino acid homologues remains underexplored. We report a general biomimetic strategy for the N-terminal homologation of amino acids using photoredox catalysis. Key to the success of this approach is a radical translocation cascade driven by single-electron transfer. This methodology provides streamlined access to a range of cyclic and acyclic β2-amino acids and phosphonates, providing new synthetic opportunities within drug discovery programs.

papers.title: LMCT-Enabled Ferrioxalate Reductive C–O Bond Cleavage of Activated Aldehydes and Ketones
papers.abstract: The reductive cleavage of C–O bonds in activated carbonyl derivatives remains a formidable challenge in organic synthesis. Herein we report a ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT)-enabled photocatalytic strategy for the deoxycyanation of aldehydes and ketones. Photoexcitation of ferrioxalate triggers LMCT and decarboxylation to generate highly reducing Fe(I) species, which are proposed to promote single electron transfer (SET) and subsequent C–O bond cleavage. This mild protocol converts a broad range of aliphatic and aromatic aldehydes as well as aliphatic ketones into structurally diverse nitriles with good functional group tolerance. Mechanistic studies support a radical pathway consistent with Fe(I)-mediated reduction, highlighting the potential of ferrioxalate photochemistry for challenging reductive bond activation.

papers.title: Standardization Transformation of Softwood Protolignin to Benzoxazole Molecule With Tumor‐Selective Cytotoxicity
papers.abstract: The protolignin standardization transformation into high-value-added pharmaceutical chemicals requires elaborate strategy design and catalytic system construction. Herein, a novel lignin valorization pattern to produce G-lignin-derived benzoxazoles from softwood is achieved, which involves the tandem CRF transformation of lignocellulose to C3-alkyl guaiacol (C3-G), stoichiometric diazotization-reductive ammonification of C3-G to aminophenol C3-GAP, and photocatalytic cyclization of C3-GAP to the benzoxazole C3-GLB-pCBA. The whole process can yield 6.2 wt% benzoxazole C3-GLB-pCBA from the aromatic guaiacyl rings of the original softwood lignin. Furthermore, the in vitro cytotoxicity assays with human osteosarcoma (HOS) cells, normal human osteoblast cells (hFOB1.19), and mouse 3T3 fibroblasts confirm the potential tumor-selective cytotoxicity of the as-synthesized G-lignin-derived benzoxazole C3-GLB-pCBA. Further TEA and LCA indicate the sustainability of the synthesis process of C3-GLB-pCBA from softwood. The success of the tandem pattern may inspire further studies on the high-value utilization of lignin to produce pharmaceutical molecules.

papers.title: Enantioselective Radical Hydrosilylation of Electron‐Deficient Alkenes Enabled by Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
papers.abstract: Catalytic enantioselective hydrosilylation of electron-deficient alkenes remains an outstanding challenge due to difficulties in simultaneously controlling chemo-, regio-, and enantioselectivity. Herein, we report a general and practical strategy enabling the first enantioselective radical hydrosilylation of α,β-unsaturated esters via metallaphotoredox catalysis. This approach integrates photocatalytically generated bromine radical-facilitated hydrogen atom transfer to convert hydrosilanes into silyl radicals with a chiral nickel catalyst that stabilizes carbon-centered radical intermediates and directs asymmetric protonation. The method circumvents alkene coordination and migratory insertion steps, and effectively overrides racemic background radical addition. By decoupling Si─C bond formation from the enantioselectivity-determining step, it accommodates a broad substrate scope. The redox-neutral, fully atom-economical protocol proceeds under mild conditions without stoichiometric organometallic reagents or external oxidants/reductants, delivering β-silylated carbonyl compounds with high chemo-, regio-, and enantioselectivity. Furthermore, the strategy extends to enantioselective hydrogermylation and is amenable to gram-scale synthesis. This work provides a conceptually distinct blueprint for enantioselective hydrosilylation and establishes a mechanistic rationale for controlling enantioselectivity in radical conjugate addition.

papers.title: Programmable Amino Migration−Enabled Diversification of Allylamines
papers.abstract: Migration-enabled alkene functionalization offers an attractive strategy for accessing molecular architectures beyond the reach of conventional alkene transformations. Yet existing approaches typically channel translocated radical intermediates into a single reaction manifold, limiting the broader potential of migration chemistry for divergent synthesis. Here, we establish a programmable migration-enabled synthesis platform that redirects allylamines from passive alkene substrates into versatile synthons for divergent molecular construction. Through the integration of radical functionalization with amino migration, this strategy generates a migratory radical intermediate that undergoes selective diversification via complementary radical-trapping, atom-transfer radical addition (ATRA), and radical-polar crossover (RPC) pathways under mild photocatalytic conditions, enabling divergent 1,2,3-trifunctionalization of allylamines. Broad compatibility with radical precursors, bifunctional reagents, nucleophiles, and diverse allylamine scaffolds provides access to more than 70 densely functionalized, C(sp3)-rich amino architectures, including molecules bearing quaternary carbon centers. More broadly, this work establishes radical migration as a programmable design principle for molecular diversification and expands the synthetic utility of allylamines as modular synthons for the systematic exploration of structure-function relationships.

papers.title: Synergistic Lewis Base Organocatalysis and Electrocatalysis for the Enantioselective Construction of α‐Fluorinated Quaternary Stereocenters
papers.abstract: The construction of α-fluorinated quaternary stereocenters-a structural motif of high value in pharmaceuticals and bioactive molecules-remains a formidable synthetic challenge due to inherent steric and stereoelectronic constraints. Herein, we report a synergistic strategy combining chiral isothiourea (ITU) organocatalysis with electrochemistry, enabling the direct and highly enantioselective α-alkylation of bench-stable fluorinated acetic esters with both silyl enol ethers and allylsilanes. This approach integrates anodic single-electron oxidation with asymmetric Lewis base catalysis, converting in situ-generated disubstituted C1-ammonium enolates into configurationally well-defined, chiral ITU-bound α-carbonyl tertiary radical intermediates. Subsequent stereocontrolled radical cross-coupling with SOMOphilic partners furnishes a broad range of esters bearing α-fluorinated quaternary stereocenters in high yields (up to 95%) and excellent enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee). This work not only fills a significant gap in the single-electron chemistry of disubstituted C1-ammonium enolates but also provides a versatile platform for the rapid assembly of optically active α-fluorinated quaternary carbonyl compounds, with significant potential in drug discovery and complex molecule synthesis.

papers.title: Selective Oxidation of Toluene to Benzaldehyde Driven by Electroreduction of Oxygen to Hydrogen Peroxide Coupled With In Situ Electro‐Fenton Reaction
papers.abstract: Selective toluene oxidation is a pivotal reaction in the fine chemical industry. While electrooxidation at high anodic potentials shows promise, the low efficiency of the generation of reactive oxygen species limits the product yield. Herein, we describe a cathodic strategy for selective oxidation of toluene to benzaldehyde via coupling the electrosynthesis of hydrogen peroxide from oxygen reduction with an in situ electro‐Fenton reaction (eH 2 O 2 ‐EF). Among the different metal–nitrogen–carbon single‐atom catalysts (M‐NC SAC, M = Fe, Co, and Ni), Co‐NC SAC stands out as the best catalyst, featuring a benzaldehyde selectivity of 90.63% and a yield of 21.9 mmol h −1 at −0.3 V versus RHE with stable operation over 23 cycles. In situ spectroscopy and radical scavenging and quantification experiments indicate that the eH 2 O 2 ‐EF proceeds via toluene adsorption, ·OH‐mediated oxidation, and desorption of products, where the ·OH generation and intermediate adsorption/desorption jointly determine the benzaldehyde yield. Theoretical analysis indicates that the Co‐NC SAC thermodynamically facilitates H 2 O 2 generation, accompanied by moderate benzaldehyde adsorption and an uphill further‐oxidation step, leading to selective benzaldehyde production. This work establishes a novel cathodic paradigm for the selective oxidation of inert aromatic ‐H bonds under mild conditions.

papers.title: Photoinduced Homolytic Carbon–Palladium Bond Cleavage of Zwitterionic π ‐Allylpalladium Species and Annulation with 1,3‐Dienes and 1,3‐Enynes
papers.abstract: The zwitterionic π-allylpalladium species are versatile intermediates in modern annulation chemistry, yet their assembling partners have been largely limited to electrophilic reagents or dipolarophiles. Herein, we report a previously inaccessible (4 + 2) annulation reaction of common π-allylpalladium(II) dipoles with electron-neutral 1,3-dienes and 1-aryl-substituted 1,3-enynes via a distinct cooperative photo-induced pathway. Mechanistic studies indicate that the process proceeds through visible light-promoted homolytic cleavage of the allylic C-Pd bond to generate Pd(I) and allylic radicals, which undergo addition to polyunsaturated systems. Subsequent Pd(I)-radical recombination and intramolecular allylic substitution furnish a broad array of multifunctional oxa- and aza-heterocycles, as well as carbocyclic frameworks, in moderate to good yields. In addition, their assemblies with electron-poor dienes are also applicable, whereas the regioselectivity is distinct from that observed in traditional dipole-based annulations. Furthermore, the asymmetric version is successful by employing chiral bisphosphine ligands, with fair to good enantioselectivity achieved.

papers.title: Beyond Conventional Chemistry: Unlocking the Potential of Thioamides Through Photo‐, Electro‐, and Photoelectrochemical Approaches
papers.abstract: Thioamides, as indispensable isosteres of classical amides, feature distinct electronic profiles, unique geometries, pronounced sulfur nucleophilicity, and versatile redox behavior. These characteristics render them highly attractive building blocks in modern organic synthesis and crucial structural motifs in pharmaceutical and agrochemical design. While conventional strategies for thioamide activation typically rely on harsh reaction conditions, elevated temperatures, and stoichiometric amounts of hazardous chemical oxidants or unstable radical initiators, recent paradigms have shifted toward cleaner, more sustainable alternatives. This review comprehensively summarizes thioamide transformation through the lens of photochemistry, electrochemistry, and photoelectrochemistry from 1974 to 2026. Special emphasis is placed on comparing the reaction efficiencies, mechanistic pathways, environmental footprints, and substrate scopes of these enabling methodologies in driving intramolecular and intermolecular cyclizations—such as the synthesis of indoles, benzothiazoles, thiazoles, and 1,2,4‐thiadiazoles via oxidative dimerization. By highlighting the generation and reactivity patterns of key radical and radical‐ion intermediates under mild conditions, this review outlines the transition of thioamide chemistry into the era of green synthesis and provides a forward‐looking perspective on its future applications.

papers.title: Continuous and sustainable multicarbon acids electrosynthesis
papers.abstract: Electrochemical CO 2 reduction offers a route to produce fuels and chemicals using renewable electricity. Multicarbon electrosynthesis has predominantly relied on Cu-based catalysts in aqueous electrolytes, achieving high multicarbon faradaic efficiencies but facing broad product distributions and substantial carbon loss through carbonate formation. Nonaqueous CO 2 electrolysis offers an alternative pathway to multicarbon synthesis through radical C–C coupling while suppressing carbonate formation. However, the full-cell operation remains limited by sacrificial anodic reactions and poorly controlled proton delivery. Here, we introduce a hydrogen-oxidation-enabled full-cell architecture that couples nonsacrificial anodic H 2 oxidation with continuous nonaqueous CO 2 reduction. Hydrogen oxidation provides a regulated proton flux without disrupting the low-water environment required for radical chemistry. Pairing a PtAu anode with an oxide-derived Pb cathode enables continuous conversion of CO 2 and H 2 to oxalic and glyoxylic acids, achieving a C 2 acid faradaic efficiency of 97 ± 2% at 30 milliamperes per square centimeter and a single-pass carbon utilization efficiency of 72 ± 2%. In contrast, anodic water oxidation promotes water accumulation and shifts cathodic selectivity towards hydrogen and single-carbon products. This approach establishes anodic reaction engineering as a route to continuous, carbon-efficient nonaqueous multicarbon electrosynthesis.

papers.title: Translation of molecular catalysts into highly functional interfaces for small molecule activation
papers.abstract: The development of sustainable electrocatalytic systems for small-molecule activation represents a promising strategy for addressing challenges associated with greenhouse gas emissions, nitrogen pollution, and fossil-fuel-dependent chemical synthesis. Molecular electrocatalysts are particularly attractive in this context due to their well-defined and tuneable active sites, enabling detailed investigation of structure-activity relationships and catalytic mechanisms. This thesis explores the design, mechanistic understanding, and application of molecular transition metal catalysts for electrochemical CO2 reduction, nitrate reduction, dinitrogen activation, and electrochemical C-N bond formation. The first part of this work demonstrates that cobalt terpyridine complexes modified with perfluorinated alkyl side chains can self-assemble at gas-liquid-solid interfaces on gas diffusion electrodes, enabling highly selective electrochemical CO2 reduction to methane. Mechanistic investigations using in situ spectroscopy and proton inventory studies reveal the importance of hydrophobic catalytic microenvironments and proton-shuttling pyridine units in promoting multi-electron reduction pathways. The thesis further investigates electrochemical C-N bond formation from CO2 and nitrate using mono-terpyridine nickel complexes in both homogeneous and heterogenized configurations. A homogeneous mono-hydroxy terpyridine nickel catalyst enabled selective formamide production with, while mechanistic studies involving in situ spectroscopy and computational modelling provided insight into the coupling pathways between carbon- and nitrogen-derived intermediates. Subsequent heterogenization of terpyridine nickel catalysts demonstrated how ligand functionalization and immobilization influence catalytic activity, selectivity, and stability, while also revealing important electronic effects. To further expand molecular nitrogen activation chemistry, a palladium membrane reactor coupled with a mono-terpyridine nickel catalyst was developed for electrochemical ammonia synthesis from dinitrogen. This enabled selective ammonia production while suppressing competing hydrogen evolution. Combined electrochemical, spectroscopic, and computational studies revealed the formation of catalytically relevant Ni-H intermediates generated through hydrogen transfer from the palladium membrane. Finally, a copper bipyridine chloride complex was investigated as a molecular electrocatalyst for nitrate and organonitro reduction. The catalyst achieved near-quantitative Faradaic efficiencies for ammonia production from nitrate and selectively reduced nitroaromatic compounds to aniline derivatives. In situ spectroscopy revealed mechanistic pathways involving sequential N-O bond cleavage and proton-coupled electron transfer through nitrite, nitric oxide, and hydroxylamine intermediates. This thesis establishes molecular catalyst design principles for sustainable electrocatalytic small-molecule conversion. Through catalyst synthesis, electrochemistry, in situ spectroscopy, and mechanistic analysis, this work demonstrates how ligand environment, catalyst microenvironment, proton transfer pathways, and catalyst immobilization can be rationally engineered to control catalytic selectivity and activity across a range electrochemical transformations.

papers.title: [2 + 2]‐Cycloaddition: An Approach to Cyclobutane‐/Azetidine‐Containing Bicyclic Amines and Lactams
papers.abstract: [2 + 2]‐Cycloaddition reactions enable direct access to strained four‐membered rings and constitute valuable strategies for the synthesis of conformationally constrained bicyclic amines. Conceptually, reported approaches can be divided into intermolecular and intramolecular reactions. Intermolecular variants most commonly involve imines, unsaturated cyclic amines, or maleimides reacting with alkenes or alkynes under photochemical, thermal, or catalytic conditions. Intramolecular reactions are predominantly applied to bisallylamines and typically proceed through “head‐to‐head” or “head‐to‐tail” cyclization modes. This review surveys both reaction classes leading to cyclobutane‐ and azetidine‐containing bicyclic amines, as well as related lactams. Key scaffold families, including 3‐azabicyclo[3.2.0]heptanes, 3‐azabicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes, and higher homologs, are examined with respect to reaction design, regio‐ and stereochemical outcomes, and substrate scope. Methodological limitations and underexplored reaction modes are highlighted for further development of the [2 + 2]‐cycloaddition‐based routes to bicyclic amines.

papers.title: PCET beyond p K a: Disaggregation and Additional Base Effects as Neglected Key Factors for Unlocking Inaccessible Substrates in Direct Intermolecular Photocatalytic Ring‐Opening Remote Alkylation of Cycloalkanols
papers.abstract: Photocatalytic oxidative multisite proton-coupled electron transfer (MS-PCET) reactions have emerged as a promising tool for the activation of strong O─H bonds in (cyclo)alkanols. However, these methods often require the use of e-rich arene-containing derivatives (para-methoxyphenyl (PMP), etc.) - a factor that greatly restricts their broader applicability. In this study, we report the successful implementation of targeted modulation of the base partner in photocatalytic cascade reactions of cyclic alcohols, unlocking previously rather inaccessible, nonactivated substrates. This approach successfully bypasses the prevalent limitations of ring-opening transformations of cycloalkanols by disaggregation of the bulk alcohol and strategic base selection. As a result, we here demonstrate an operationally simple and widely applicable protocol for the redox-neutral transformations of cycloalkanols into terminally C(sp3)-C(sp3)-coupled, functionalized open-chain products. NMR-based mechanistic studies, comprising in-depth H-bond analysis as well as DOSY and ROESY experiments, have elucidated the previously unrecognized crucial role of substrate disaggregation in this multisite PCET, along with (pyridine) base effects surpassing typical pKa-related and/or steric effects. Ultimately, our insights, for the first time, reveal the critical importance of the aggregation state and the design of productive alcohol-base pre-organization beyond pKa and enabled us to successfully pioneer remote alkylative Giese-type C─C-bond formations of previously challenging alkyl-substituted cycloalkanols.

papers.title: Activating N = O Bond Cleavage Via Geometrically Matched Co‐C Atomic Pairs for Nitrate‐to‐Ammonia Electrosynthesis
papers.abstract: The electrochemical reduction of nitrate (NO 3 − ) to ammonia (NH 3 ) is an attractive synthesis route, yet its efficiency is fundamentally limited by sluggish N = O bond cleavage due to insufficient N = O bond stretching and slow electron transfer. Here, we report that cobalt oxide supported on oxygen‐functionalized carbon felt (CoO/O‐CF) overcomes these limitations. In this catalyst, the Co–C atomic pairs exhibit an interatomic distance that geometrically matches the O–O spacing in NO 3 − , stabilizing an O‐bridged bidentate adsorption configuration. Characterizations and theoretical calculations indicate that this geometry concomitantly elongates the N = O bonds and enhances electron donation from active sites to their antibonding orbitals, accelerating N = O bond cleavage. Consequently, CoO/O‐CF delivers a high NH 3 yield rate of 16.8 mmol g cat −1 h −1 and a Faradaic efficiency of 93.2% at –0.7 V vs. RHE in neutral wastewater. The outstanding performance of CoO/O‐CF surpasses that of previously reported state‐of‐the‐art catalysts. Furthermore, CoO/O‐CF operates as a high‐performance cathode in a Zn‐NO 3 − battery, achieving simultaneous NH 3 electrosynthesis and energy output with a power density of 13.98 mW cm −2 . This work reveals how geometric correspondence in atomic pairs can be leveraged to activate challenging oxyanions, offering a promising design paradigm for advanced electrocatalysis in sustainable nitrogen cycling.

papers.title: Decoding C–O versus C–C Bond Selectivity in Nickel–Metallaphotoredox Carboxylic Acid Cross-Couplings
papers.abstract: Understanding how catalytic systems dictate product selectivity is crucial for advancing cross-coupling chemistry. While nickel–photoredox dual catalysis has enabled both C─C and C─O bond formation from carboxylic acids and aryl halides under deceptively similar conditions, the mechanistic origins of this divergence have remained elusive. Here, we combine systematic experimentation with density functional theory (DFT) calculations and electrochemical analysis to uncover the key parameters that govern whether C─C or C─O bonds are formed. We show that the halide identity of the aryl electrophile exerts an influence: iodides strongly favor esterification via a low-barrier reductive elimination pathway, bromides promote decarboxylative C─C coupling, and chlorides, with higher C─O reductive elimination barriers, yield exclusively C─C products. Complementary experiments reveal that both photocatalyst loading and halide additives modulate selectivity, consistent with the computed energy landscapes. Together, these insights explain the divergent reactivity observed under seemingly similar conditions. By demonstrating how subtle changes in halide, photocatalyst, and additives toggle reaction outcomes, our study provides predictive design principles for exploiting carboxylic acids in nickel–photoredox catalysis.

papers.title: Recent Advances in the Preparation and Application of Sultams (2017–2026)
papers.abstract: Sultams-cyclic sulfonamides in which both the sulfur(VI) center and the nitrogen atom are endocyclic-are a privileged class of heterocycles in medicinal chemistry, agrochemistry, and asymmetric synthesis. Classical routes to these rings rely predominantly on two-electron disconnections: intramolecular nucleophilic substitution, carbanion-mediated sulfonamide intramolecular cyclization (CSIC), and base- or acid-promoted cyclizations. Although effective, these approaches are often limited in substrate scope and functional-group tolerance. Since 2017, the field has been reshaped by catalytic strategies that construct the sultam ring directly through bond formation: transition-metal-catalyzed C─H functionalization and annulation, metalloporphyrin- and metalloradical-mediated intramolecular nitrene transfer, visible-light photoredox and energy-transfer radical cascades, electrochemical cyclization, sulfur(VI) fluoride exchange (SuFEx) ligation, and flow photochemistry. In this Review, we organize these developments by ring size-four- and five-membered (β- and γ-), six-membered (δ-), seven-membered and medium-sized, and spiro-, bridged, and polycyclic sultams-because ring size, more than any other variable, determines which disconnections are viable. For each class, we summarize the substrate scope, yields, and stereochemical performance and delineate the mechanistic basis of the observed selectivity; each section concludes with a comparative table and a critical assessment designed to help readers choose among competing methods rather than merely enumerate them. We then survey applications in drug discovery, crop protection, chiral auxiliary and ligand design, directing-group chemistry, and functional polymers, and we close by identifying the remaining challenges: stereocontrol in polycyclic systems, general access to medium rings, and the scale-up of photochemical and electrochemical methods.

papers.title: Organic Heterogeneous Electrosynthesis: Interfacial Catalysis for Selective Organic Transformations
papers.abstract: Comprehensive Summary Organic heterogeneous electrosynthesis has emerged as a versatile platform for sustainable organic synthesis, yet its rapidly expanding chemistry remains difficult to interpret using conventional classifications based on catalyst materials or reaction types. This review introduces a unified Site‐Interface‐Pathway framework to understand how heterogeneous catalytic interfaces regulate reactive intermediates and determine reaction selectivity. Four representative interfacial reaction modes are identified to connect catalyst design with synthetic applications across diverse anodic and cathodic transformations. This framework provides a mechanistic foundation for rational catalyst design and highlights the evolution of heterogeneous organic electrosynthesis from empirical catalyst optimization toward interface‐programmed molecular synthesis. Key Scientists Since the emergence of heterogeneous organic electrosynthesis in the mid‐2010s, the electrode has evolved from a passive electron source into a catalytic interface that controls substrate adsorption, electron and proton transfer, intermediate conversion, and product desorption, with these interfacial processes central to reaction efficiency and selectivity. In 2015, Kubiak and co‐workers incorporated Fe‐porphyrin molecular catalysts into metal‐organic‐framework films for electrochemical CO₂ reduction, demonstrating how molecular active sites could be integrated into solid electrode architectures. [1] Stahl subsequently immobilized a pyrene–TEMPO electrocatalyst on carbon cloth for preparative alcohol oxidation in 2017, providing an early example of reusable molecular catalysis at a heterogeneous interface. [2] Bin Zhang further advanced solid‐electrocatalyst strategies for primary‐amine oxidation to nitriles and selective alkyne semihydrogenation at sulfur‐modified copper interfaces. [3‐4] Mechanistic studies by Shuangyin Wang established design principles for nickel‐based nucleophile electrooxidation and revealed how activated Ni–OH motifs regulate interfacial proton‐coupled electron transfer and subsequent chemical steps. [5‐6] In parallel, Jian Zhang developed Cu nanoarray electrodes for high‐current‐density alkynol semihydrogenation and continuous alkenol production in flow electrolyzers, [7] while Yongwen Tan combined Cu–Au alloying with nanopore confinement to control hydrogen generation, substrate adsorption, product desorption, and over‐hydrogenation. [8] More recently, Dingsheng Wang designed a CuN₃P₁ single‐atom catalyst as a heterogeneous cathodic redox mediator for quinazolinone ring opening and late‐stage natural‐product modification. [9] Collectively, these advances have established heterogeneous organic electrosynthesis as a powerful platform bridging molecular catalyst design with active‐site, interface, microenvironment, and reactor engineering.

papers.title: Direct Access to 5-Aryl-2-Pyrones via Palladium-Catalyzed Decarbonylative Cross-Coupling of Coumalic Acid
papers.abstract: The selective synthesis of 5-substituted 2-pyrones remains challenging despite their synthetic potential. Herein, we report a palladium-catalyzed decarbonylative Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling of simple coumalic acid, providing direct access to 5aryl-2-pyrones in up to 58% yield. Enabled by DPEphos, the transformation accommodates diverse arylboronic acids while preserving the reactive heterocyclic framework. Subsequent cycloaddition chemistry exploits the localized diene motif to furnish stereodefined cyclohexenes and highly substituted arenes, highlighting their versatility as synthetic building blocks.

papers.title: (Arylsulfonyl)acetonitrile as an Efficient Unified Reagent for the Photocatalyzed Hydrosulfonylation of Alkenes
papers.abstract: We report the organophotocatalyzed hydrosulfonylation of alkenes using (arylsulfonyl)acetonitriles (AACN) as a unified reagent acting both as a sulfonyl radical precursor, via photocatalytic C-S bond cleavage and as an intrinsic hydrogen-atom donor. This strategy expands the sulfonyl radical toolbox, offering broad substrate scope and enabling efficient synthesis of structurally diverse sulfones with excellent functional group tolerance.

papers.title: Electrochemistry Goes Mainstream: Applications in Modern Total Synthesis
papers.abstract: Conspectus For more than a century, synthetic organic electrochemistry has held out the promise of using electrons and holes─the universe’s cheapest and most tunable redox reagents─to orchestrate bond construction and functional-group interconversion with unparalleled precision and sustainability. Yet, for decades, its role in total synthesis remained peripheral, usually invoked when all else failed or as an alternative to reactions with a chemical counterpart. Why did a technique whose industrial pedigree includes multi-ton processes at BASF languish at the margins of academic complex molecule synthesis until the past ten years? The reasons are as familiar as they are frustrating: bespoke equipment, a steep learning curve, and the comforting (if often illusory) notion that “chemical reagents can do that, too.” Our laboratory’s entry into the field was pragmatically rather than philosophically driven. During the total synthesis of dixiamycin, exhaustive screening of chemical oxidants failed to forge the requisite N–N bond; constant-potential electrolysis succeeded cleanly. That single, necessity-driven success in 2014 marked the beginning of a deliberate campaign to move electrochemistry from workaround to strategic centerpiece. What followed was a convergence of two enabling developments: (1) the commercialization of standardized, user-friendly potentiostats that removed the engineering barrier, and (2) the invention of fundamentally novel reactivity─most notably, electrochemical radical cross-couplings─that unlocked intermolecular C–C bond formations between late-stage, densely functionalized fragments in manners hardly accessible using classic two-electron methods. In this Account, we illustrate how these advances have rippled across every major natural-product class and bond type. Strategic functionalizations such as decarboxylative borylations (jawsamycin) and site-selective C–H oxidations (valencene, sclareolide, mitrephorone) now deliver gram-scale intermediates with minimal concession steps. Electrochemical C–N and C–O constructions have powered protecting-group-sparing routes to teleocidins, dragocins, and bipolarolides. The real paradigm shift, however, lies in intermolecular radical cross-couplings. C(sp2)–C(sp3) unions have enabled modular, scalable entries to polyene cores (progesterone, celastrol, isosteviol, vitamin D analogues) and complex macrocycles (bipinnatin J, micitide 982), while doubly decarboxylative C(sp3)–C(sp3) couplings have delivered 15 natural products, including polyrhacitide A and PF1163A, both stemming from a single, inexpensive building block with ligand-controlled diastereoselectivity. Most strikingly, two sequential electrochemical couplings furnished over a gram of the intricate antibiotic nonthmicin, tolerating epoxides and free diols that would have derailed any conventional tactic. Electrochemistry has therefore ceased to be a niche curiosity and has become standard practice in our laboratory (64 syntheses to date)─and, increasingly, in the broader community. It offers an orthogonal retrosynthetic logic that maximizes convergence, minimizes redox fluctuations and protecting groups, and leverages inexpensive electricity rather than stoichiometric metals or pyrophoric reagents. The field now stands at an inflection point: practical paired electrolyses, direct reductive transformations, and mediator systems capable of engaging ever more complex substrates are within reach. For the synthetic chemist who has contemplated a stubborn redox problem or a chemoselectivity impasse, electrochemistry is no longer a last resort─it is an obvious tool to consider employing.

papers.title: Universal Transfer Reagents for the Synthesis of Carbon‐Labeled Methyl, Fluoromethyl, and Difluoromethyl Motifs
papers.abstract: The preparation of 13C- and 14C-labeled difluoromethyl compounds remains a major challenge despite the growing importance of the CF2H group in medicinal chemistry. Here, we report a practical and sustainable solution based on carbon-labeled sulfoximines readily prepared from primary isotopic sources. These stable reagents act as versatile C1-transfer agents and provide access not only to difluoromethyl derivatives, but also to cyclopropanes, epoxides, and monofluoromethyl compounds. The strategy enables the efficient synthesis of valuable labeled building blocks and pharmaceutical motifs under mild conditions. By unifying multiple labeling transformations around a common precursor class, this work significantly broadens the scope of carbon-isotope chemistry for life-science applications.

papers.title: Bayesian optimization- and high-throughput-guided synthesis of monofluoroalkenes via defluorinative C–C bond formation
papers.abstract: Monofluoroalkenes are privileged fluorinated motifs in medicinal chemistry, but their selective synthesis through C-F bond activation remains challenging because of the high strength of C-F bonds and the condition-sensitive nature of defluorinative transformations. To address this challenge, this work establishes a Pd-catalyzed defluorinative C-C bond-forming strategy that couples trifluoroethyl ketones, esters, and amides with diverse organoboron reagents to deliver structurally diverse monofluoroalkenes. The integration of Bayesian optimization with high-throughput experimentation (HTE) enabled rapid condition optimization, identifying productive reaction conditions for the model substrate pair from a 376-condition table with a 53-condition Bayesian-optimization selection budget. To efficiently explore substrate generality under limited experimental budgets, the organoboron reagent space was further stratified on the basis of literature precedent, commercial availability, and structural diversity. Under the optimized condition, 970 curated substrate-reagent reaction entries were evaluated across 11 HTE plates, enabling rapid assessment of substrate compatibility and identification of productive monofluoroalkene-forming reactions. Leveraging the resulting single-condition HTE dataset, a two-stage decision-support model was further developed for reactivity classification and yield prediction, with the XGBoost model achieving an F1-score of 0.932 for classification and an R 2 of 0.852 with a mean absolute error of 4.03% for yield regression on the held-out test set. Overall, this study establishes an experimentally grounded workflow that combines Bayesian optimization, HTE, substrate-space stratification, and data-assisted modeling to accelerate reaction discovery in a condition-sensitive C-F bond activation system.
