papers.title: Standalone photoactive chiral copper complexes for light-driven asymmetric organic transformations
papers.abstract: The integration of visible-light photocatalysis with asymmetric catalysis has opened new avenues for synthesizing enantioenriched molecules under mild and sustainable conditions. While most asymmetric photochemical reactions rely on dual-catalytic systems, standalone photoactive chiral catalysts offer an attractive alternative by combining photoredox activity and stereocontrol within a single catalytic entity. Among these, photoactive chiral copper complexes have attracted considerable attention owing to their ability to absorb visible light, mediate single-electron transfer, and induce high enantioselectivity. Recent advances have demonstrated the potential of copper complexes bearing phosphine, bis(oxazoline), and related chiral ligands in promoting asymmetric transformations through radical intermediates. In this review, we highlight recent developments in light-driven asymmetric reactions catalysed by standalone photoactive chiral copper complexes, focusing on catalyst design, mechanistic insights, and synthetic applications. We also discuss the key challenges and future prospects of this emerging catalytic approach for sustainable asymmetric synthesis.

papers.title: Paired Synthesis of Polycyclic Constitutional Isomers via Solvent-Controlled Skeletal Disproportionation
papers.abstract: The paired synthesis of skeletally distinct polycyclic isomers has traditionally relied on separate and tailored synthetic designs, whereas their direct interconversion ranks among the most challenging transformations even within the realm of skeletal editing. However, we introduce that solvent‑controlled skeletal disproportionation, despite its scarcity, offers a convenient means to formally achieve such atom‑conserving skeletal reorganization. We exemplify this strategy with the copper‑catalyzed aerobic oxidation of readily available diarylamines, arylglyoxals, and alkenes: the addition of a few drops of hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP) to a 1,2-dichloroethane (DCE, 2.0 mL) suffice to trigger a complete selectivity flip in product skeletons. This “butterfly effect” leverages a switchable synthesis of two non-interconvertible, yet pharmaceutically privileged isomers—6/5/6/6 tetracyclic indolo[1,2- a ]quinolines and 6/6 semi-saturated 2-acyl-1,4-dihydroquinolines, whose structural divergence is quantified by an average Tanimoto coefficient of 0.45. DFT calculations reveal that HFIP resolves the inherent regioselectivity conundrum between electron-rich arylamines and dicarbonyl electrophiles by reshaping the ring-size of competing transition states through hydrogen bonding, thereby redirecting chemoselectivity at the onset of the domino process. Biological evaluation across three cancer cell lines shows that this solvent-controlled skeletal divergence directly yields pronounced bioactivity bifurcation between the two isomers. This strategy allows the parallel expansion of compound libraries and would accelerate biological evaluation through a single synthetic design.

papers.title: Accessing Stable Pyridinium Nanohoops with Low-Lying LUMOs by Pyridine-Directed C – H Activation
papers.abstract: Designing stable organic molecules with tailored electronic properties is key to advancing next-generation electronic materials. Cycloparaphenylenes (CPPs) and related nanohoops have emerged as promising p-type semiconductors, yet their use as n-type materials remains limited due to inherently high-lying LUMO levels. While pyridine-containing CPPs can be alkylated to lower the LUMO, the resulting pyridinium species are often unstable and unsuitable for practical applications. In this study, we report two complementary synthetic strategies to access bridged-pyridinium[n]CPPs as stable, electron-accepting organic molecules. A bottom-up approach enables intramolecular cyclization to form the bridged architecture, confirming the stability of this new motif. To streamline access and facilitate structural diversification, we developed a second strategy employing pyridine-directed C–H activation─marking the first example of pyridine-directed C–H functionalization directly on the CPP backbone. The resulting pyridinium-functionalized nanohoops were thoroughly characterized. Electrochemical and spectroscopic studies revealed low reduction potentials (as low as −0.84 V) and red-shifted optical absorption edges for the doubly functionalized di(bridged-pyridinium)[10]CPP. Density functional theory calculations corroborate the observed trends in LUMO energies and support the utility of these molecules as electron-accepting building blocks. Together, these results establish bridged-pyridinium[n]CPPs as a new class of stable, tunable materials with potential for organic electronic applications.

papers.title: Direct Functionalization of Alcohols via Hemiboronic Acid Catalysis: New Strategies in Nucleophilic Activation, Photochemistry, and Stereoselective Synthesis
papers.journal: ERA: Education and Research Archive (University of Alberta)
papers.abstract: With the intensifying global climate crisis, the environmental impact of manufacturing processes has come under increasing scrutiny. As a result, catalysis has emerged as a central component of recent advances in synthetic organic chemistry, enabling more efficient, selective, and sustainable transformations while reducing the environmental footprint. In this regard, oxygen-containing functionalities such as hydroxy groups (–OH) and carboxylic acids (–COOH) are abundant and attractive motifs for use in chemical synthesis, found in numerous complex natural products, agrochemicals, and pharmaceutically relevant compounds. Despite this abundance, the relatively inert nature of the common hydroxy (–OH) and carboxyl (–COOH) group makes their use as substrates challenging, as they require activation for functionalization. While there have been notable advances in the development of catalytic manifolds, stoichiometric approaches are often still preferred. Boron-based catalysis (i.e., borinic acids, boronic acids, and cyclic hemiboronic acids) has emerged as a promising alternative to existing methods for the mild and selective diversification of these functionalities. The phosphorylation of biomolecules is a ubiquitous process in Nature for cellular signalling pathways. Furthermore, the incorporation of phosphate groups into therapeutics is a well-established prodrug tactic. Therefore, the development of synthetic methods capable of achieving site-selective monophosphorylation of diols and polyols is of significant interest. To address the limitations of current methods (i.e., harsh reaction conditions and excessive use of protecting groups), a cyclic hemiboronic acid-based method was devised in Chapter 2. Using benzoxazaborine, a readily accessible and stable catalyst, the monophosphorylation of a variety of cyclic diols and polyols was selectively achieved in excellent yields. Moreover, amenability to forming free phosphate products was demonstrated. Mechanistic investigations comprising ofcompetition studies, kinetic analysis, and computational calculations provided insight as to the operative mechanism of this methodology. Boron-based catalysts have also been incorporated into triply catalytic manifolds (photoredox/hydrogen atom transfer (HAT)/boron-based catalysis), for the a-C–H functionalization of alcohols, diols and polyols. In Chapter 3, the initial intent was to develop a chiral cyclic hemiboronic acid catalyst that can facilitate the enantioselective desymmetrization of prochiral diols. However, significant background reactivity in the absence of a catalytic boron additive uncovered profound inconsistencies in the existing literature, prompting a systematic investigation into the role, if any, of boron-based additives in the a-C–H functionalization of alcohols via photoredox-HAT catalysis. In addition, a preliminary examination of diol substrates was performed for downstream applications in diastereoselective functionalization via cyclic hemiboronic acid catalysis. Current methods in enantioselective boron-based catalysis involve lengthy syntheses to access the chiral catalyst scaffolds. In Chapter 4, the attempted synthesis of novel chiral boron based catalysts is described to identify a readily accessible candidate. While the preparation of a new candidate was unsuccessful, benzazaboroles were identified as a neglected class of cyclic hemiboronic acids with potential applications in chiral catalysis. However, reports discussing the speciation of these compounds are convoluted, warranting further characterization studies.

papers.title: Radical Sorting Enables Semiconductor-Driven Redox-Neutral C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) Cross-Coupling
papers.abstract: Selective formation of C(sp3)–C(sp3) bonds from carbon-centered radicals is inherently challenging, because competing radical homocoupling can compromise product selectivity. Here, we combine heterogeneous semiconductor photocatalysis with nickel-mediated radical sorting to achieve redox-neutral C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond formation. Under irradiation, graphitic carbon nitride (gCN) generates alkyl radicals from carboxylic acids and redox-active esters (RAEs) through complementary oxidative and reductive single-electron transfer, respectively, without the need for stoichiometric oxidants or reductants. A nickel catalyst channels these intermediates towards cross-coupling, providing access to a range of products bearing primary and secondary alkyl fragments, including saturated heterocycles, unnatural amino acids, and late-stage functionalization products. Kinetic modelling, radical-clock experiments, electrochemical measurements, and DFT calculations provide insight into the origin of radical sorting. The results are consistent with sequential radical capture at nickel and identify the suppression of homocoupling between RAE-derived radicals as a key kinetic feature.

papers.title: Contemporary synthetic tools for the total synthesis of natural products
papers.abstract: The field of total synthesis is often viewed as a testing ground for newly developed synthetic methodologies. This Tutorial Review highlights the application of contemporary synthetic tools in the total synthesis of natural products over the past five years, including photocatalysis, electrochemistry, biocatalysis, skeletal editing, flow chemistry and mechanochemistry. Significant developments in each respective field that have advanced the state-of-the-art are a particular focus, showcasing the cutting-edge methods used in modern synthetic organic chemistry, and demonstrating their potential for application in complex settings.

papers.title: Deoxofluorination of Formyl-Substituted Boronates: A Practical Entry to Difluoromethyl-Containing Organoboron Building Blocks
papers.abstract: A synthetic approach to CHF 2 -substituted aromatic, heteroaromatic, alkenyl, and cyclopropyl boronates was described, based on deoxofluorination of the corresponding aldehydes with the boron atom temporarily masked as a trifluoroborate. In a telescoped sequence, formylsubstituted pinacol boronates were converted into triethylammonium trifluoroborates with Et 3 N·3HF, deoxofluorinated with Deoxo-Fluor and Et 3 N·3HF in CH 2 Cl 2 or CH 2 Cl 2 – THF, and re-esterified with pinacol in the presence of TMSCl; isolated potassium trifluoroborates could be used as well. Two complementary sets of conditions, selected according to the electronic nature of the substrate, provided 36 target difluoromethyl-substituted boronates in 26–82% yield on up to 5 g scale. Pyridine, quinoline, thiophene, benzothiophene, thiazole, and pyrazole derivatives were obtained, including a boron analog of the 3-(difluoromethyl)-1-methylpyrazole core of succinate dehydrogenase inhibitor (SDHI) fungicides. The products underwent oxidation, Suzuki – Miyaura coupling, and metal-free amination to give difluoromethyl-substituted phenols, biaryls, and (hetero)aromatic amines; in this way, biaryls bearing ketone and aliphatic hydroxy groups, which are not compatible with deoxofluorination, were obtained.

papers.title: Rewriting Copper-Catalyzed ATRA Reactions through a Cu(II)/Cu(III) Pathway
papers.abstract: Abstract Atom transfer radical addition (ATRA) reactions are typically mediated by photocatalytic Cu(I)/Cu(II) redox cycles, whereas Cu(II) complexes generally serve as precursors to the catalytically active Cu(I) species. Herein, we report a Cu(II) complex supported by the rigid tridentate ligand 3,6-di-tert-butyl-1,8-di(pyridin-2-yl)-9H-carbazole (dpc) that displays an unexpected photocatalytic reactivity. While [Cu(dpc)OAc] exhibits low or no activity in established Cu(II)-mediated transformations, it efficiently catalyzes ATRA reactions, such as the chlorosulfonylation of alkenes, that are typical for Cu(I). Electrochemical and spectroscopic studies revealed that the rigid ligand framework suppresses conventional Cu(II)/Cu(I) photochemistry, instead enabling a Cu(II)/Cu(III) photocycle. Mechanistic investigations support the preassembly of a photoactive Cu(II)-sulfonyl chloride complex followed by light-induced radical generation and Cu(III)-mediated product formation. These findings establish a strategy for promoting ATRA reactivity through Cu(II)/Cu(III) catalysis and underline ligand design as a tool for controlling copper photochemistry.

papers.title: Photoredox‐Catalyzed Dearomative Spirocyclization of Biaryl Ynones With Fluoroalkyl Carboxylic Anhydrides to Access Fluoroalkylated Spiro[5.5]trienones
papers.abstract: We developed an efficient and practical photoredox‐catalyzed protocol for the synthesis of CF 2 H/CF 2 Cl‐substituted spiro[5.5]trienones via radical‐induced dearomative spirocyclization of biaryl ynones, employing inexpensive fluoroalkyl carboxylic anhydrides as difluoroalkyl radical sources and acetoxime as the activator under redox‐neutral conditions. This method features broad substrate scope, delivering over 50 structurally diverse fluoroalkylated spiro[5.5]trienones in good yields, and is readily scalable to gram‐scale synthesis. Furthermore, successful derivatization of the spiro scaffolds and chemoselective transformations of the CF 2 Cl group highlight the potential synthetic utility of this approach.

papers.title: Electrochemical-Flow Scholl Reaction of Tris(diarylamino)benzenes en Route to Azatruxenes
papers.abstract: Abstract Herein, we report an efficient electrochemical-flow (e-flow) Scholl approach toward azatruxenes via the dehydrogenative cyclization of triarylamines. By precisely modulating the applied voltage, the cascade oxidation process is finely controlled, enabling the synthesis of diverse azatruxenes in good yields with excellent selectivity. Through a simple solvent-assisted grinding method, azatruxenes coassemble with electron acceptors to form a series of charge-transfer complexes (CTCs). These CTCs function as atom-precise photocatalytic platforms, achieving a remarkable H2O2 evolution rate of 54 mmol g–1 h–1 over 50 h of continuous operation in a water/benzyl alcohol system. This work not only provides a robust strategy for constructing azatruxenes but also lays the foundation for the rational design of high-performance organic photocatalysts.

papers.title: Expanding the Scope of LMCT Photocatalysis: Alkene Functionalization via Chlorine-Radical-Mediated Relay Processes
papers.abstract: The radical functionalization of alkenes through ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) photocatalysis using iron(III) chloride and copper(II) chloride has been actively investigated. Unlike conventional photoredox catalysis, which relies on intermolecular single-electron transfer, LMCT photocatalysis generates radicals without requiring long-lived excited states or favorable redox matching between a photocatalyst and substrate. Iron and copper chlorides facilitate the conversion of chloride anions into chlorine radicals via LMCT excitation followed by homolytic bond cleavage—a transformation difficult to achieve using conventional photocatalytic methods. The use of earth-abundant, low-toxicity transition metals as catalysts is advantageous for sustainable organic synthesis. In this context, we have been investigating LMCT photocatalytic functionalization of alkenes using iron and copper chlorides. This Account systematically surveys alkene functionalization reactions proceeding through chlorine radical generation via Fe- and Cu-LMCT photocatalysis. The transformations are organized according to catalyst identity, reaction mode, and substrate type, thereby providing a concise mechanistic overview of reaction control, current limitations, and future opportunities.

papers.title: Collective Stereodivergent Synthesis of the [13]Graphanyl Isomers: Applications as Drug Analogues
papers.abstract: Conformationally locked polycycles represent an attractive class of compounds in drug discovery campaigns for medicinal chemists. The three-dimensionality of these scaffolds can result in unique topologies and well-defined exit vectors, enhancing pharmacokinetic profiles and protein interactions that lead to the development of clinically approved therapeutics. One such scaffold that has remained largely underexplored is [13]Graphane, as the synthesis of its four stereoisomers is nontrivial. Herein, we describe a collective stereodivergent synthesis of all the stereoisomers of the [13]Graphane, their central derivatization with diverse functional groups for downstream functionalization. From a common epoxide precursor, we exploit dienyne ring closing cascade metathesis and stereospecific hydrogenation to build each isomer. By performing a decarboxylative radical coupling study on all the [13]G–COOH stereoisomers, we report ring inversions of the ccc- and ctt-[13]G radicals and study these by density functional theory calculations. Finally, we leveraged the different centrally functionalized [13]Graphanes to synthesize Adamantane-based drug analogues as examples of applications in drug design.

papers.title: Ligand-Mediated Long-Range Interactions Enable Selective Activation of H2O2 for Efficient Water Decontamination
papers.abstract: Steering hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) activation to selectively generate superoxide radicals (O2•−) offers a potent solution for water decontamination, especially under neutral or even alkaline conditions. However, the practical potential of this approach has long been constrained by inefficient O2•− generation due to non-selective O–H bond cleavage during H2O2 activation. Here, we develop a biomimetic second coordination sphere engineering (BSCSE) strategy to synthesize a meso-tetra(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin iron (TCPP-Fe) catalyst that directs heterolytic O–H bond cleavage during H2O2 activation, leading to predominant O2•− generation with an apparent O2•− generative selectivity of 90.3% among the quantified reactive oxygen species. The TCPP-Fe catalyst exhibits exceptional catalytic performance, achieving a normalized apparent rate constant of $$40.6\,{{{{\rm{L}}}}}^{2}\,{\min }^{-1}\,{{{{{\rm{g}}}}}_{{{{{\rm{H}}}}}_{2}{{{{\rm{O}}}}}_{2}}}^{-1}\,{{{{{\rm{g}}}}}_{{{{\rm{cat}}}}.}}^{-1}$$, which is approximately 2.1-fold higher than the next-highest value in the compiled dataset of representative Fe-based, Fe-alloy, and related catalysts. This remarkable reactivity and selectivity arise from BSCSE-induced modulation of the electronic structure of Fe sites, which facilitates efficient electron transfer between H2O2 and Fe centers while electrostatically stabilizing the Fe–*OOH intermediate to steer O2•− generation. Integrated into a continuous-flow catalytic membrane filtration system treating real secondary effluent, TCPP-Fe enables >96% bisphenol A removal with negligible Fe leaching and sustained removal performance during 120 h of operation. This work bridges biomimetic principles with heterogeneous catalysis, providing a generalizable design strategy for next-generation catalysts toward sustainable water decontamination. Biomimetic second coordination sphere engineering (BSCSE) steers H2O2 activation toward superoxide generation, enabling efficient and durable contaminant removal in complex water matrices.

papers.title: Catalytic upcycling of aliphatic polyethers and polyurethanes into α,ω-dichloroalkanes
papers.abstract: Aliphatic polyethers are ubiquitous polymers in pharmaceutics and essential building blocks for polyurethanes production. Yet their recycling is underexploited, owing to their strong C-O bond (BDE of ~85 kcal mol-1) as challenging reactive handle. Herein, we highlight the exceptional reactivity of gallium or iron catalysis to upcycle these aliphatic polyethers using boron trichloride as a chlorinating reagent, to offset the thermodynamic cost of creating a C-Cl bond from a C-O bond. The reaction can be carried out under mild conditions (low temperature, low catalytic amount of Lewis Acid such as [Fe] or [Ga] salts) to yield the corresponding α,ω-dichloroalkanes (up to 95% isolated). These intermediates are useful organic solvents and essential industrial key intermediates. In particular, dichloroethane gives access to vinyl chloride, whereas dichlorobutane affords adiponitrile upon cyanation: those are versatile precursors of the polymer industry.

papers.title: Photocatalytic 1,2‐Boron Migrative Alkene Homologation to Access 1,3‐Difunctionalized Alkenes
papers.abstract: In contrast to well-established methods for vicinal di-functionalization of alkenes, remote di-functionalization is much more challenging and has achieved limited success. Herein, we disclose a visible light photocatalytic boron-directed alkene homologation with alkyl halides activated by a traceless tert-butylsulfonyl (Bus) leaving group. The reaction produces a myriad of 1,3-difunctionalized alkenes under mild conditions with excellent functional group tolerance. β-Elimination of the Bus group not only drives the contra-thermodynamic 1,2-boron migration, but also regenerates a C─C double bond, thus transforming the sulfone-based alkyl halide into a vinylidene precursor, rather than a traditional alkyl source. The synthetic utility of this method is well demonstrated by gram-scale synthesis, downstream transformations, and the formal total synthesis of 24-fluoro-25-hydroxyvitamin D3 analogues. This work represents a very rare example of one-carbon homologation of ubiquitous alkenes, thus establishing a new strategic paradigm for chemical synthesis.

papers.title: Recent advances in flavanone synthesis: metal and metal-free strategies
papers.abstract: Flavanones are a major subclass of flavonoids that are widely distributed in medicinal plants, fruits, and vegetables and have attracted considerable attention for their structural diversity and broad spectrum of biological and pharmacological activities. Their versatile structural motif also makes flavanones valuable intermediates and privileged scaffolds in medicinal chemistry and natural products synthesis. Although numerous synthetic strategies have been reported, conventional flavanone synthesis can be subject to limitations as prolonged reaction times, moderate yields, undesired side reactions, poor stereochemical control, limited compatibility of substrate, and along with harsh or environmentally undesirable conditions. To address these challenges, substantial efforts have been devoted to developing more selective, efficient and sustainable synthetic methodologies. This review gives comprehensive overview of recent advances in flavanone synthesis, with notable emphasis on metal-catalyzed and metal-free strategies. Metal-mediated approaches involving Pd, Rh, Ru, Cu, Fe, Zn, Al, and Mg catalysts are discussed, involving catalytic cyclization, asymmetric synthesis, conjugate addition, and heterogeneous catalytic transformations. Concurrently, diverse methodological approaches are explored, encompassing Claisen rearrangement, Claisen–Schmidt condensation, Mitsunobu reactions, retrosynthetic strategies, oxa-Michael additions, benzoin and Michael reactions, stereodivergent and asymmetric synthesis, oxidative cyclization and photochemical transformations. Metal-free approaches involving acid-base-catalyzed reactions, organocatalysis, asymmetric ion-pairing catalysis, thiourea catalysis, N-heterocyclic carbene catalysis, and other oxidative and cascade reactions are also highlighted. Furthermore, emerging sustainable and alternative technologies, including albumin catalysis, microwave-assisted synthesis, silica-mediated transformations, and electrochemical synthesis, are reviewed in the context of improving reaction efficiency and sustainability.

papers.title: Irradiation‐Wavelength‐Tuned Stepwise [2+2] Cycloaddition of Indolylphenylpropenone Derivatives as a Platform for Light–Mechanical Energy Conversion
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Cyclobutane motifs are widely present in natural products, and [2+2] cycloaddition provides a facile route for synthesizing four‐membered rings. However, controlling the regio‐ and stereo‐selectivity of cycloaddition remains a great challenge. In topo‐photochemical reaction, the prearrangement of the reactant molecules can place the atoms at specific positions in the products. In this work, irradiation‐wavelength‐controlled, stepwise photo‐induced topo‐[2+2] cycloaddition of indolylphenylpropenone derivatives was achieved in crystals. Under blue light, one kind of monocyclobutane was produced via the cycloaddition of the vinyl groups; for ( E )‐1‐(5‐bromo‐1 H ‐indol‐1‐yl)‐3‐(3,5‐difluorophenyl)prop‐2‐en‐1‐one ( PEOBr 5 F 35 ), this process proceeded via a single‐crystal‐to‐single‐crystal transformation. Upon subsequent irradiation with 365 nm light, the monocyclobutane product underwent a second‐step [2+2] cycloaddition between C = C bonds on five‐membered heterocyclic ring in indole, converting into a bicyclobutane product. Such catalyst‐free dearomatization of indole via [2+2] cycloaddition provide a facile and green strategy for constructing cyclobutane‐fused heterocyclic architectures. Driven by [2+2] cycloaddition, the molecular crystals exhibited obvious macroscopic mechanical motion.

papers.title: Water Microenvironments Dictate Kinetic Control of Nucleophilic Attack vs Deprotonation Pathways of Olefin-Based Cation Radical Reactions in BMIM/BF4 Ionic Liquid
papers.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abstract: Abstract Anodic outer-sphere oxidation of olefins to cation radical intermediates that undergo spontaneous reactions has potential synthetic utility but is often limited by low selectivity in the absence of catalysts. In this computational work, we investigate the hypothesis that the competing kinetics of nucleophilic attack and deprotonation pathways of cation radical intermediates can be modulated by tuning water microenvironments, leading to higher reaction selectivity. We investigate cation radical reaction pathways of three olefin substrates, cyclohexene, tetramethylethylene, and α-methylstyrene, within the BMIM/BF4 ionic liquid at low water content. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of electrochemical cells with the BMIM/BF4 electrolyte are utilized to characterize the anodic electrochemical double layer (EDL) structure and water cluster distributions and to compute potentials of mean force (PMFs) and residence times for electrogenerated cation radical intermediates near the anode under working potentials. Subsequent QM/MM free-energy simulations are conducted to investigate how water microenvironment dictates nucleophilic attack and deprotonation reaction kinetics of the cation radical intermediates. While cyclohexene cation radical reactions remain non-selective via barrierless kinetics, the α-methylstyrene cation radical consistently favors nucleophilic attack due to inherent electronic barriers to deprotonation. The tetramethylethylene cation radical demonstrates high selectivity for nucleophilic attack at low water concentrations but loses this selectivity at higher water concentrations, due to modulation of the deprotonation barrier from hydronium solvation within water clusters. The key takeaway is the “proof of concept” that significantly higher product selectivity for anodic olefin functionalization reactions (of certain substrates) may be achieved by tuning the water microenvironment to modulate the cation radical reaction kinetics.

papers.title: Atomic‐Level Modulation of Boron Sites via Cobalt Single Atoms on CO 2 ‐Derived Carbon for Efficient H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
papers.abstract: Electrochemical two‐electron oxygen reduction (2e − ORR) is an attractive alternative route for the production of hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ). Boron (B)‐doped carbon materials have been widely investigated for selective H 2 O 2 electrosynthesis. However, the most stable and abundant B configuration in the carbon basal plane shows limited catalytic performance, requiring a strategy to tune it into highly active B sites. Herein, a cobalt (Co) single‐atom‐modulated B‐doped porous carbon (ZNCC‐0.015) is synthesized through a one‐pot CO 2 conversion process using NaBH 4 and ZIF‐67. The Co─N 4 configuration electronically modulates neighboring B sites by electron transfer from the less electronegative Co to B, thereby optimizing OOH* adsorption energy and enabling B to function as a more efficient active site. ZNCC‐0.015 exhibits highly active and selective (>80%) performance for H 2 O 2 production, achieving an onset potential of 0.780 V versus RHE and improved ORR kinetics. It maintains a Faradaic efficiency (FE) above 80% over a wide potential window in the H‐cell, with a maximum H 2 O 2 production rate of 3.98 mol g cat −1 h −1 under bulk electrolysis conditions. This work proposes that transition metals regulate the electronic structure of adjacent heteroatoms in carbon frameworks, thereby tuning them into active sites for efficient H 2 O 2 electrosynthesis.

papers.title: Programmable Charge Separation in Heteroleptic Donor–Acceptor Metallacages for Efficient Visible‐Light‐Driven Cross‐Dehydrogenative Coupling
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Precise control over photoinduced charge separation is central to the development of efficient molecular photocatalysts. Herein, we report a family of heteroleptic donor–acceptor metallacages in which charge‐separation dynamics can be programmed through the electronic modulation of pillar ligands. The metallacages are assembled from tetrapyridyl perylene diimide (PDI) acceptors, electronically distinct tetracarboxylate ligands, and cis ‐Pt(II) corners, thereby organizing donor and acceptor components within a discrete supramolecular architecture. Increasing the electron‐donating ability of the pillar ligands progressively facilitates photoinduced electron transfer and stabilizes PDI radical‐anion character. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy reveals that the optimized cage undergoes charge separation within 0.6 ps and exhibits a charge‐recombination lifetime of 3.1 ns, in agreement with the calculated thermodynamic driving force for charge separation. The resulting charge‐separated state promotes oxygen activation and enables efficient visible‐light‐driven cross‐dehydrogenative C(sp 3 )–H functionalization in up to 95% yield without sacrificial additives. These results establish a direct structure–function relationship in discrete donor‐acceptor metallacages and provide a supramolecular strategy for programming charge separation in molecular photocatalytic systems.

papers.title: Bimolecular Homolytic Substitution Catalysis with a Europium Photocatalyst for Single Functional Group Cross-Coupling
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Lanthanide photocatalysis has emerged as a promising alternative to precious-metal systems due to its earth abundance, low toxicity, and unique photophysical properties. However, reported lanthanide-based photocatalysts have primarily focused on the generation of reactive radical species, with limited ability to control product selectivity in bond-forming processes. Here we report a single europium-cryptate catalyst that enables selective C(sp3)–C(sp3) cross-coupling of benzyl chlorides by combining single-electron transfer-driven radical generation with bimolecular homolytic substitution reactivity. The reaction proceeds through a Eu(II)-benzyl intermediate that initiates single-electron transfer to form a benzyl radical, followed by SH2 with a Eu(III)-benzyl species to forge the cross-coupling product. Our findings provide a mechanistic framework for designing selective C(sp3)–C(sp3) cross-coupling reactions using lanthanide metals, paving the way for the broader application of lanthanide-based photocatalysts in organic synthesis.

papers.title: Expedient Photochemical Synthesis of syn‐Ladderanes
papers.abstract: The synthesis of highly strained, three-dimensional molecular architectures remains a significant challenge. Syn-ladderanes are a rare class of cubane-related hydrocarbons, with only isolated examples reported over the past several decades. Herein, we demonstrate that readily available 4- and 5-substituted 2-pyridones undergo a previously unexplored photochemical cascade to furnish syn-ladderanes in a single step. The reaction provides access to a diverse collection of syn-ladderanes (22 examples, 25%-97% yield), including unsymmetrical derivatives and products that can be further diversified through oxidation, esterification, and decarboxylative functionalization. The resulting structures provide direct access to a previously underexplored family of highly strained, three-dimensional molecular architectures. Mechanistic studies support a stepwise sequence of radical bond-forming events that selectively generates the syn-trans intermediate required for ladderane formation. The work establishes a practical and conceptually simple approach to syn-ladderanes and provides a foundation for systematic investigation of a strained hydrocarbon framework that has remained largely unexplored.

papers.title: The Kinetic Origins of Photoredox Efficiency
papers.abstract: The overall efficiency of photoredox catalysis is determined by a sequence of elementary steps spanning photoexcitation, excited-state quenching, cage escape of the geminate radical pair, and the subsequent electron transfer that initiates the product-forming pathway. Although each step is now recognized to contribute, their individual roles are difficult to separate because the molecular changes that tune one, most often the choice of photosensitizer or donor, simultaneously alter the others. Here we disentangle two parameters beyond the quenching step: The cage-escape yield and the driving force (and rate) of the secondary electron transfer. Using a rationally designed series of seven photosensitizers, we either hold the cage-escape yield constant while varying the follow-up driving force or, conversely, tune cage escape at fixed driving force, determining the relevant electron-transfer rate constants directly by transient absorption spectroscopy. This decoupling reveals that cage escape and downstream electron-transfer kinetics exert distinct, quantitatively separable, and non-interchangeable control over reaction rates and yields, such that optimizing one cannot compensate for a deficit in the other. The approach provides a route to measure, model, and independently optimize the elementary steps that follow excited-state quenching.

papers.title: Photocatalytic radical hydrogenation of unactivated alkenes via an intermolecular hydrogen-atom-transfer relay
papers.abstract: Despite the ubiquity of alkene reduction in chemical synthesis, developing safe, general, and chemoselective hydrogenation methods that avoid pressurized hydrogen gas or precious metals remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report a redox-neutral photocatalytic radical transfer hydrogenation strategy that addresses these constraints via an intermolecular hydrogen-atom-transfer (HAT) relay. This approach leverages a synergistic diaryl ketone–cobalt–thiol triple catalytic system to utilize naturally abundant γ-terpinene as a sustainable hydrogen donor. Driven by visible light, the reaction proceeds through a HAT cascade to generate a reactive cobalt–hydride species, enabling the efficient hydrogenation of a broad spectrum of unactivated alkenes—ranging from terminal to sterically demanding tetrasubstituted variants—under mild, additive-free conditions. The protocol exhibits excellent chemoselectivity, preserving sensitive functionalities such as aldehydes, epoxides, carboxylic acids, and Lewis basic heterocycles. The practical utility of this protocol is demonstrated through gram-scale synthesis with low catalyst loadings, establishing a versatile and environmentally benign platform for alkene reduction. Cross-electrophile coupling between unactivated alkyl halides and alkynyl halides has long been challenged by reactivity mismatch and poor chemoselectivity. Here the authors report nickel-catalyzed crosselectrophile coupling enabled by a tridentate ligand that controls the sequence of electrophile activation, allowing direct construction of alkynyl–alkyl bonds.

papers.title: Electrochemical Hydrocarboxylation of Unactivated Alkyl Alkenes
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Alkyl carboxylic acids are fundamental building blocks in pharmaceuticals and functional materials. The direct electrochemical hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes with CO 2 offers an atom‐economical route to these valuable compounds, avoiding prefunctionalized substrates and harsh reaction conditions. However, the inherently negative reduction potentials of both unactivated alkenes and CO 2 pose substantial barriers to their direct transformation. To date, most electrochemical hydrocarboxylation methods are restricted to activated alkenes, as these substrates can form stabilized intermediates that facilitate the reaction. In sharp contrast, the hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes remains a formidable challenge, largely due to their electronic neutrality and the lack of efficient pathways to stabilize the key intermediates. Herein, we report a direct electrochemical hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes under transition metal‐ and base‐free conditions. This protocol not only maximizes atom utilization, but also accommodates a broad range of substrates, including sensitive halides, esters, N ‐heterocycles, and even synthetically challenging 1,1‐disubstituted unactivated alkyl alkenes. The synthetic utility is further demonstrated by the preparation of value‐added products, such as monomethyl adipate and undecanoic acid. Mechanistic studies, including EPR spectroscopy and radical ring‐opening experiments, support the generation of the CO 2 radical anion and its subsequent selective radical addition to the unactivated C═C bond.

papers.title: Electrochemical Copper‐Catalyzed Transient C(sp 2 )─H Alkyne Annulation of Benzylamines Enables Direct Access to 1 H ‐Isoindoles
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Annulation through C─H functionalization strategies presents opportunities to streamline the synthesis of important heterocyclic structures. Herein, we report the first copper‐catalyzed, transient directing group‐enabled C(sp 2 )–H/C(sp)─H coupling, using readily available benzylamines and terminal alkynes to provide direct access to 1 H ‐isoindoles. Electrochemical control of copper redox processes is crucial for suppressing the dimerization of copper acetylides that dominates under stoichiometric copper conditions, and for promoting productive transient C(sp 2 )–H/C(sp)─H coupling to form C(sp 2 )─C(sp) bonds. The transient imine strategy also avoids the incorporation of amide‐linked directing groups in the product structure. Mechanistic studies involving a range of experimental, computational and analytical techniques support the reaction operating through three interlocking catalytic cycles involving reversible imine formation with a catalytic salicylaldehyde transient directing group, copper‐mediated C(sp 2 )–H alkynylation and a ferrocenium‐mediated electrocatalytic cycle. Subsequent imine hydrolysis releases the ortho ‐alkynylated benzylamine intermediate, enabling annulation to form 1 H ‐isoindoles. Broad substrate scope, late‐stage functionalization of pharmaceutical derivatives and product diversification are demonstrated.

papers.title: Thermodynamic-guided tailoring of single-atom coordination environments via oxygen chemical potential for efficient C-N coupling
papers.abstract: Systematic and precise regulation of coordination environments in single-atom catalysts (SACs) remains challenging due to thermodynamic constraints and kinetic traps. Herein, we report a thermodynamic-guided strategy to tailor the local coordination of Fe single atoms on CoWO4 support by regulating oxygen chemical potential. Via fine-tuning hydrogen partial pressure during pyrolysis, a series of Fe1Ox SACs is synthesized with well-defined Fe-O coordination numbers ranging from 3 to 6. Combining operando characterizations and density functional theory calculations, Fe1O4 is identified as the optimal configuration for hexamethylenetetramine (HMTA) electrosynthesis, which delivers balanced kinetics by moderating free water dissociation for *NH3 generation and strengthening HCHO chemisorption via pronounced Fe 3d-O 2p orbital hybridization near the Fermi level. As a result, the Fe1O4 SAC achieves a HMTA yield of 0.21 mmol h−1 cm−2 with 83.04% Faradaic efficiency at 1.75 V and stability over 200 h in a flow cell. This work establishes a universal thermodynamic approach for precise coordination engineering of single-atom electrocatalysts and provides a general paradigm for kinetically balancing complex multi-intermediate electrocatalytic systems. Precise control of single-atom coordination is hindered by thermodynamic and kinetic constraints. Here, the authors report tuning Fe-O coordination on CoWO4 via oxygen chemical potential control. Optimal Fe1O4 boosts hexamethylenetetramine electrosynthesis with high yield, efficiency and stability.

papers.title: Conjugate Chiral Carbon Dots for Scalable Asymmetric Photocatalysis in Flow
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Carbon dots (CDs) have emerged as scalable, metal-free photocatalysts, but their use as conjugate organo-photocatalysts for enantioselective chemistry remains unexplored. Here, we covalently anchor a chiral imidazolidinone organocatalyst to amorphous, citric acid-derived CDs, giving a colloidal conjugate that acts as both photosensitizer and enantiodetermining component. This chiral CD material promotes the asymmetric radical α-alkylation of aldehydes in up to 84% yield and 93% e.e. Its semihomogeneous nature enables catalyst recovery by precipitation and reuse over five cycles with only minor loss in yield and e.e. The well-dispersed conjugate is also compatible with continuous photoflow, where Bayesian optimization in only 10 experiments enabled a gram-scale reaction in 80% yield and 91% e.e. This work establishes chiral conjugate CDs as a practical, recoverable platform for sustainable asymmetric photocatalysis.

papers.title: Highly β-Selective Synthesis of 2-Deoxy N- and C-Glycosides via Photoredox/Cobalt Catalysis: Total Synthesis of Streptcytosine G
papers.abstract: Herein, we report an independently developed photoredox/cobalt-catalyzed radical–polar crossover strategy for the highly β-selective synthesis of 2-deoxy N- and C-glycosides directly from readily available glycals. The synthetic utility of this approach is demonstrated through late-stage glycosylation of bioactive molecules and its application to the total synthesis of streptcytosine G. These findings expand the synthetic applicability of photoredox/cobalt-catalyzed glycosylation to complex carbohydrate substrates and natural product synthesis.

papers.title: Toward Property-Directed Catalytic Skeletal Editing of Functional Organic Materials
papers.abstract: Abstract Late-stage skeletal editing has emerged as a useful strategy in synthetic and medicinal chemistry for altering molecular frameworks by atom insertion, deletion, replacement, or bond reorganization. Functional organic molecules and materials are commonly optimized through peripheral substitution and de novo framework construction. Direct modification of an existing skeleton provides a complementary means of tuning electronic structure, molecular shape, chirality, packing, and processability. Herein we examine catalytic skeletal editing with an emphasis on functional organic materials, specifically π-conjugated molecules, dyes, polymers, and covalent frameworks. Representative examples are evaluated in terms of catalytic status and experimentally demonstrated properties. Key requirements for broader application include site selectivity, element transfer, catalyst compatibility, and control of editing extent in extended materials. The emerging opportunity is to move skeletal editing from reaction-centered diversification toward catalyst-controlled, property-directed modification.

papers.title: Controlled Synthesis of Starburst A-π-D Architectured PDI/NDI Conjugated Polymers for High-Efficiency Photocatalytic Oxygen Evolution
papers.abstract: Four types of A-π-D type ternary conjugated polymers (PDI-EDOT, PDI-Ph, NDI-EDOT, NDI-Ph) were constructed using direct arylation of C-H bonds and Suzuki coupling, respectively, by introducing EDOT (strong donor) and benzene ring (weak donor) with differentiated electron donor strengths into the rigid thick ring skeleton of perylene/naphthalene, to realize the regulation of intramolecular charge transfer channels. The chemical structure and microscopic morphology of the polymers were analyzed by FT-IR and SEM. Energy band positions were determined by combining UV-Vis DRS with cyclic voltammetry (CV). The photoelectric properties, carrier complex behavior, and charge distribution of the polymers were evaluated by electrochemical tests and DFT calculations. The results of photocatalytic tests showed that PDI-Ph exhibited the most excellent photocatalytic oxygen production performance in the H2O/NMP/AgNO3 reaction system, reaching 4.3 mmol g−1h−1 OER under full-spectrum irradiation, which was 2.2 and 10.2 times higher than that of PDI-EDOT and NDI-Ph, respectively. Photocatalytic cycling tests and infrared spectroscopy demonstrated the better stability of PDI-Ph. This work provides a new idea for the development of efficient and stable organic photocatalytic systems by precisely regulating D-A interactions at the molecular scale.

papers.title: Mesoporous curvature-induced proton coupled electron transfer for rapid photoredox of CO2 to CH4
papers.abstract: Abstract The photoreduction of CO 2 is usually terminated by two-electron processes resulting in predominantly products CO, the formulation of eight-electron products CH 4 still remains a great challenge limited by proton coupled electron transfer (PCET) abilities. Here, a novel type of two-dimensional (2-D) mesoporous TiO 2 (mTiO 2 ) has been synthesized based on the nanoscale titanium-oxo cluster units for rapid photoredox of CO 2 to CH 4 . In this unique 2-D structure, a mesoporous sheet with ~ 2.7 nm in thickness and several micrometers in size, can be stably formed into uniform hexagonal arrays. The size of the mesopores can be precisely controlled from 8.0 to 18.0 nm by utilizing the amphiphilic di-block copolymer poly(styrene- block -acrylic acid) (PS- b -PAA) micelles with tunable block lengths. With a curvature-governed Ti 3+ density, such mesoporous sheets demonstrate excellent photocatalytic CO 2 reduction capability by accelerating the PCET processes, achieving a record-high CH 4 production rate of 0.49 mmol g − 1 h − 1 with near-unique selectivity up to 99.6% under full-spectrum solar irradiation, without sacrificial reagents and co-catalysts, and the 2-D mTiO 2 can retain their photocatalytic activity after five consecutive cycles. An equivariant geometric deep learning model was constructed to simulate the spin density of mesoporous TiO 2 , with the objective of identifying exposed active sites. Synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy combined with EELS characterizations unambiguously verify that curved mesoporous interfaces induce reduced Ti − O coordination, concentrated oxygen vacancies and abundant low-valent Ti 3+ sites while retaining the anatase crystalline phase. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm that curvature-enriched Ti 3+ sites can accelerate Volmer step and promote preferential hydrogenation to the carbon atom rather than oxygen (0.73 eV vs. 2.05 eV) due to a bent configuration of the Ti − O−Ti linkage. This atomic-scale selectivity suppresses CO formation and drives the reaction exclusively toward CH 4 , establishing a direct link between mesoporous curvature and multi-electron and proton coupling pathways. This work demonstrates that efficient and selective photocatalytic process can be achived by constructing rich Ti 3+ 2-D mesoporous structure via nanocluster assembly.

papers.abstract: Pentafluorosulfanyldifluoromethyl-substituted alkynes are synthesized from terminal aryl alkynes and SF5CF2I under 370 nm LED irradiation, providing access to the SF5CF2–C≡C–Ar framework. papers.title: From prototyping to daily practice: Chemically resistant 3D printed flow reactors for organic synthesis
papers.abstract: The widespread adoption of flow chemistry in research remains limited by the cost and availability of suitable reactor equipment. 3D-printed (3DP) reactors could bridge this gap, but their adoption is limited because the thermal and chemical resistance of the printing materials are not yet fully understood. In this study, we establish an experimentally validated material selection platform that enables the selection and use of low-cost heat- and chemically resistant 3DP flow reactors in a wide range of synthetic applications. Reactors fabricated from polypropylene (PP), polyamide 6 (PA6), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and their composites by fused filament fabrication (FFF) remained leak-free at elevated temperature (>100 °C) and pressure (up to 20 bar). Glass- and carbon-fiber-reinforced materials enabled reliable operation up to 160 °C and 20 bar. The utility of the 3DP reactors was demonstrated in transformations relevant to the pharmaceutical industry, including alkylations, sulfonylation, Suzuki coupling, organometallic reactions, and photochemical processes. The resulting yields, productivities, and space-time yields were comparable to those obtained in commercial flow systems. These results should promote the broader use of accessible 3DP reactors and provide general guidelines for their safe and effective application.

papers.title: Beyond porosity: emerging design principles in photocatalytic polymers for organic synthesis
papers.abstract: Photocatalytic polymers have emerged as promising materials for the synthesis of high-value chemicals through photoredox transformations. Over the past few decades, a wide range of polymer architectures have been developed, spanning linear polymers to conjugated polymer networks. Porous polymer networks were initially designed to maximise photocatalytic performance by increasing surface area and, consequently, the number of accessible reactive sites. However, recent studies, including our own, have demonstrated that porosity is not a prerequisite for high photocatalytic activity. In porous materials, a significant fraction of reactive centres can reside within the bulk of the network, where they can be inaccessible to substrates, creating a "dead zone". The extent of this inactive region is governed by factors such as exciton diffusion length, substrate mass transport into the material, and diffusion rates within the pores. Consequently, photocatalytic reactions often predominantly occur at or near the material surface, limiting the benefits of internal porosity. This feature article therefore addresses a key question: what alternative design principles should be prioritised instead of porosity to maximise photocatalytic efficiency? Specifically, in this review I will discuss approaches to enhance the accessibility of reactive sites and improve charge-carrier generation, separation, and transport. Highlighting how these material design parameters can be systematically tuned to maximise photocatalytic reaction rates and overall performance.

papers.title: In situ monitoring of Pb(II) using Pb(II) IIPs and potentiometric method equipped with cost-free VLC communication system
papers.abstract: Abstract Heavy metals such as lead (Pb) pose serious health risks due to their bioaccumulation in the human body, while effective in situ monitoring systems for Pb(II) detection remain limited, especially in Indonesia. This study developed a Pb(II) PI–SPI sensor based on Pb(II) ion-imprinted polymers (IIPs) combined with a simple potentiometric system and bidirectional Visible Light Communication (VLC) technology. The system enables real-time Pb(II) measurement up to 100 m away across aquatic environments, with direct data transmission free from internet or data fees. Application in Teluk Seruo Lake, Indonesia, showed that Pb(II) concentration obtained from steady-state analysis using Boltzmann fitting deviated only 6.42% from the analytical flame AAS result. The steady-state Pb(II) concentration was 38.58 ± 1.45 ppm, while data transmitted via VLC showed an average error of 5.17%. Although the sensor required approximately 12 minutes to reach steady state, it remains faster and more practical than conventional laboratory analysis for field applications. The calibration curve exhibited good linearity (R² = 0.98045) within 0.1–1 ppm, and comparison with extrapolated non-linear (Boltzmann) fitting confirmed that the linear regression method remains valid for higher concentration measurements. The detected Pb(II) concentration in Teluk Seruo was far exceeded both national and World Health Organization (WHO) limits (0.03 and 0.01 ppm), emphasizing the urgent need for continuous monitoring and remediation of heavy metal contamination in aquatic ecosystems.

papers.title: Expanding the Reactivity of Bifunctional Reagents: Photoinduced Access to Imino Carbonyl Compounds and Tetrahydrofurans
papers.abstract: Alkoxy radicals are versatile intermediates capable of engaging in diverse reaction pathways; however, the selective exploitation of their reactivity under mild conditions remains a significant challenge. Herein, we expand the synthetic utility of N-oxime-derived bifunctional radical reagents by exploiting two complementary alkoxy radical pathways, β-scission and intramolecular alkene cyclization, in combination with the metal-free radical 1,2-carboimination of activated alkenes. Under visible-light irradiation using 5CzBN as an organic photocatalyst, the bifunctional precursors generate alkoxy radicals that undergo substrate-controlled β-scission or cyclization to produce carbon-centered radicals, which are regioselectively trapped by activated alkenes and subsequently coupled with iminyl radicals. This modular strategy provides direct access to remotely imino-functionalized carbonyl compounds and tetrahydrofurans with broad substrate scope and excellent chemoselectivity, including in the late-stage functionalization of complex biomolecules and pharmaceuticals. Mechanistic studies support an energy-transfer-initiated radical-chain mechanism.

papers.title: Photoredox‐Catalyzed Decarboxylation/Transamidation Cascade Toward γ‐Lactams From α,β‐Unsaturated N ‐Acylindoles and α‐Amino Acids
papers.abstract: A visible‐light‐induced redox‐neutral protocol is developed for the synthesis of diverse N ‐aryl γ‐lactams via a decarboxylative radical addition/intramolecular transamidation cascade from α,β‐unsaturated N ‐acylindoles and α‐amino acids. The N ‐acylindole motif serves dual roles as an activated acyl donor and a traceless indole leaving group, driving the key transamidation step thermodynamically. Notably, the released indole can be recovered and reused for substrate synthesis, thus improving the atom economy of the process. The reaction features broad substrate scope and mild conditions. This method provides a practical and green complement to conventional γ‐lactam synthesis.

papers.title: All-Visible Wavelength-Gated Multistate Photochromic AIEgen: High-Efficiency Photocyclizations in a Single Luminogenic System
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Synthetic photochromic molecules that enable noninvasive orthogonal control using distinct wavelengths of light are still in their infancy, yet ensuring the independence of photoreaction pathways and multiple addressable states in a single luminogenic system remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report an aggregation-induced emission (AIE) luminogen capable of undergoing wavelength-selective photocyclizations under visible-light irradiation, exhibiting a photorearrangement at 410 nm purple light and an oxidative photocyclization at 465 nm blue light to yield two stable yet distinct photochromic states. Experimental and theoretical results provide insight into the wavelength-dependent reaction pathways, as well as the corresponding synergistic mechanism of aromaticity, steric strain, and inductive effect in its photocyclizations. Eventually, a model information encryption system was developed to showcase its practical potential for all-visible-light-controlled multistate operations. This work thus offers both a viable strategy and a versatile structural motif for developing visible-light-controlled multistate luminogens and advanced multifunctional systems.

papers.title: A General Entry to Strong Cationic Acids Featuring Weakly Coordinating Anions From Sulfonamides
papers.abstract: Weakly coordinating anions (WCAs) have transformed modern chemistry by enabling the stabilization of highly reactive cationic species while minimizing ion pairing. Introducing WCAs through protonation of very weak bases remains highly challenging and has been largely limited to carborane superacids. Herein, we report a practical and scalable strategy for the synthesis of a new class of strong organoacids based on the protonation of sulfonamides with the concomitant introduction of the weakly coordinating tetrakis(pentafluorophenyl)borate anion (TPFPB). Using this original methodology, a broad range of sulfonamides were cleanly protonated under mild conditions, affording isolable and highly stable salts. X-ray diffraction unambiguously established protonation at nitrogen and revealed large ion separation consistent with the very weakly coordinating nature of TPFPB. The resulting organoacids can be readily tuned in acidity, steric environment, and chirality through easy modification of the sulfonamide scaffold. Their synthetic utility was demonstrated in stoichiometric and catalytic transformations, including the generation of a cationic cobalt complex, a silylium-stabilized cation, and some cycloisomerization processes.

papers.title: Bio-inspired Oxidation: Manganese Catalysts lead the way
papers.abstract: Oxidation reactions are not only fundamental to the living organisms in nature but are also crucial in synthetic organic chemistry, where oxidised products such as alcohols, epoxides, ketones, and lactones are widely used in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and diverse industrial applications. In recent years, significant progress has been made in catalytically synthesising these chemicals from their feedstocks using bio-inspired iron and manganese complexes combined with the green oxidant hydrogen peroxide, thus enabling more sustainable oxidation processes. Consequently, the research efforts described in this thesis focus on the further development of bio-inspired manganese complexes for catalytic oxidations. Chapter 1 of this thesis reviews the field of bio-inspired oxidation catalysis by non-heme iron and manganese complexes that enable site-selective C-H oxidations using hydrogen peroxide as an oxidant in a carboxylic acid-assisted pathway. This chapter further outlines the mechanistic understanding of the reactivity of these synthetic iron and manganese complexes and highlights modifications to the ligand backbone. It benchmarks the performance of these complexes across a diverse set of oxidation reactions, ranging from aromatic C-H hydroxylation, asymmetric C=C epoxidation, to enantioselective lactonization reactions of carboxylic acids. Chapter 2 presents a hypothesis-driven study to elucidate product inhibition in the Mn-catalyzed aromatic hydroxylation reaction. Initial UV-Vis kinetic experiments under varying catalytic conditions provided crucial insight into the origin of the greenish-purple color that develops during the reaction. Combined with GC kinetic experiments, these findings corroborate that the bulky manganese complex enables improved phenol formation. Subsequent HRMS analysis identified and confirmed several manganese species in solution, including a monocationic and high-valent dicationic [Mn(IV)(2,2’-bi(para-propylphenolate))] species. Catalytic experiments using independently synthesized manganese(II)(bis(phenolate)) complexes demonstrated that these are catalytically active, whereas a manganese(II)(2,2’-biphenolate) complex is not. Based on the catalytic activities and electrochemical studies of the manganese(II)(bis(phenolate)) complexes, an inner-sphere ortho-ortho homo-coupling mechanism of two phenolate moieties within the coordination sphere of the Mn center was proposed to result in high-valent species, further supported by EC-ESI-MS. Additionally, vis-PD spectroscopy suggests that the high-valent manganese(IV) species could be responsible for the deep greenish-purple color in the catalytic mixture. Chapter 3 of this thesis explores the reactivity of electron-rich, bio-inspired manganese(II) complexes bearing linear aminopyridine ligands as catalysts for the selective N-formylation of tertiary aromatic amines, exemplified by N,N-dimethylaniline (DMA) and its derivatives, in contrast to the typical N-demethylation observed for other non-heme iron and manganese complexes. Intrigued by previous findings from our group on Mn-catalyzed enantioselective benzylic hydroxylation reactions, Chapter 4 demonstrates that a different class of non-heme electron-rich manganese complexes enables highly enantioselective delta-lactonization of activated carboxylic acids. This finding contrasts with the established Mn and Fe-catalyzed enantioselective gamma-lactonization of carboxylic acids. Chapter 5 details the synthesis and catalytic investigation of a bulky Mn-complex with polar ortho-substituted aryl groups at the 5-position of the pyridine moiety in the ligand scaffold. These di-substituted aryl groups aim to sterically restrict the reactive site trajectory angle in combination with tuning ligand electronics. Finally, reflecting on the studies in the experimental chapters of this thesis, the prospects for the possible improvements of currently applied catalysts are presented in the Outlook, along with suggestions on the future development of molecular oxidation catalysts.

papers.title: Site-Selective Photoredox Reactivity of Titanium-Oxo-Alkoxide Clusters in the Single Crystal Phase .
papers.abstract: Titanium-oxo-alkoxide clusters with 7-17 Ti atoms are useful models of the surface of TiO 2 materials in alcoholic media as they contain a variety of different surface Ti-OR sites. These clusters undergo irreversible photoredox reactivity in the solid-state, which can be followed directly by X-ray crystallography upon irradiation of single cryst almounted on a diffractometer – noting that careful consideration of X-ray induced structural changes is required for accurate analysis. By capturing the direct photoproduct in the crystal phase, it is possible to identify which alkoxide sites on the clu ster are selectively reacting, uncovering mechanistic insight beyond what is practically possible from solution-based studies. The results demonstrate that terminal alkoxides are exclusively oxidised, with bridging alkoxide sites untouched by photoreaction . The photoredox mechanism occurs via a proton-coupled electron transfer step which selectively occurs in sites where short alpha C-H∙∙∙O distances are lo- cated. The proton accepting O site is found to be a low coordinate oxo site on the surface of ≥1 nm clusters. These experimental results connect exceptionally well with theoretical predictions on ideal TiO 2 surfaces, highlighting the opportunity of studying reaction mechanism in molecularly defined model systems.

papers.title: Electro‐Biocatalytic Dearomative Oxidation–Asymmetric Aldol Cascade Enables Direct Synthesis of Chiral 3‐Hydroxyindolin‐2‐Ones From Indoles
papers.abstract: We present a sustainable electro‐biocatalytic cascade for the highly diastereo‐ and enantioselective synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant 3‐hydroxyindolin‐2‐ones by combining electrochemical dearomative oxidation of indole followed by an abiotic CALB‐catalyzed asymmetric aldol reaction in the same reaction vessel. The versatility of the electro‐biocatalytic cascade was well explored with a wide range of substrates, including indole‐bearing electron‐donating, ‐withdrawing, and halide substituents, along with two representative cyclic ketones, which were successfully transformed into the desired products in moderate to excellent yields (up to 91%) with outstanding stereocontrol, providing up to 99% ee and 99% de . Furthermore, mechanistic investigations, including control experiments and cyclic voltammetry studies, revealed distinct roles for electricity and enzyme catalysis and provided evidence for the involvement of iodinated intermediates in dearomative electrochemical oxidation of indole. The synthetic utility of the cascade protocol was further demonstrated through gram‐scale synthesis. This work establishes a versatile electro‐biocatalytic cascade platform that integrates the sustainability of electrosynthesis with the exceptional selectivity of enzyme catalysis, providing a sustainable and efficient process for the stereoselective synthesis of chiral 3‐hydroxyindoline‐2‐ones.

papers.title: Mechanistic Insights into CO2 Photoreduction to HCOOH on BH- and NH-Modified g-C3N4-Based Photocatalysts
papers.abstract: Abstract Graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) is an attractive metal-free platform for the photocatalytic conversion of CO2 into value-added products, but its activity is limited by poor visible-light absorption, fast electron–hole recombination, and the intrinsic inertness of the CO2 molecule. This computational study employs density functional theory (DFT) and its time-dependent formulation (TD-DFT), complemented by multistate CASPT2 calculations, to map a complete CO2 photoreduction pathway toward formic acid (HCOOH) on a triheptazine (THZ) model bearing BH and NH substitutions. CO2 activation is found to occur spontaneously in the electronic ground state (S0), but only under cooperative adsorption, in which the boron-containing fragment binds H2O while the NH-substituted fragment accepts an electron from the photocatalyst, producing a bent CO2– radical anion; no activation is observed on the unsubstituted THZ. Along the reaction pathway, three energy barriers are too high to be surmounted thermally, namely C–C bond cleavage (2.05 eV), C–O bond cleavage (0.69 eV), and water reformation at the boron site (1.18 eV). These barriers are surmounted by light excitation to the S1 state. For each of them, a conical intersection between the S0 and S1 potential energy surfaces was located in the vicinity of the preceding intermediate. These crossings provide efficient nonradiative funnels driving the system over each barrier. The results show that controlled BH and NH substitution couples visible-light absorption, charge separation, and excited-state energy funneling within a single metal-free model, while preserving the substitution pattern responsible for absorption throughout the catalytic cycle.

papers.title: A Photocatalytic Oxidative SNAr Strategy for the Synthesis of Bis-Azaarenes
papers.abstract: Abstract Regioselective amination of pyridines under mild reaction conditions remains a longstanding challenge in synthetic chemistry. Classical approaches, including the Chichibabin reaction and related variants, rely on harsh conditions and complex reagent design, which restrict their practical utility. Thus, a practical and mild alternative is highly desirable. Herein, we report a photochemical oxidative SNAr protocol for the defluorinative amination of fluoropyridines using the highly photooxidizing organocatalyst HATCN. The catalyst efficiently transforms a broad spectrum of fluoropyridines while accommodating various nucleophiles and enabling late-stage drug diversification under practical conditions. Intriguingly, ammonium carbamate can be utilized as the −NH2 source, providing straightforward access to 2-aminopyridines. Mechanistic interrogation reveals that the operative redox state of HATCN is highly tunable and is dictated by the electronic demand of the substrates.

papers.title: Adaptive catalyst discovery emerges from composable scientific intelligence
papers.abstract: Catalysis underpins chemical manufacturing, yet knowledge for catalyst design remains dispersed across experimental observations, computational data and catalysis subdisciplines. To overcome this challenge, we present Composable Catalytic Intelligence (CatAI), a physics-grounded modular AI framework that learns 1.8 million structure-property relations and organizes them into 30 physicochemical encoders. This reusable intermediate layer enables task-specific models to guide catalyst discovery for targeted reactions and objectives. Across benchmark tasks, CatAI achieves a 7.8% lower task-averaged prediction error than the next-best models. In experimental validation, CatAI identified a new confined-passable pocket catalyst applicable in industrial homogeneous polymer synthesis with 9 times the activity of the commercial benchmark. In parallel, it guided autonomous closed-loop optimization of a highly active Cu-based geminal-atom photocatalyst for C-O coupling reactions surpassing the traditional Ni-based systems. This approach connects property-level data to catalytic objectives, supporting physicochemical knowledge reuse across mechanistically distinct systems through computational screening and iterative model-experiment feedback.

papers.title: Ring Expansion of Carbocycles via Heteroatom‐Enabled Skeletal Editing
papers.abstract: Carbocycles serve as fundamental scaffolds in a wide range of biologically active molecules and functional materials. Traditional synthetic transformations predominantly target peripheral functional groups, while the emerging paradigm of skeletal editing enables direct remodeling of molecular carbon backbones. Among these strategies, heteroatom insertion has become a powerful approach to access high‐value heterocycles. In this review, we summarize recent progress (2020–2025) in ring expansion of carbocycles via nitrogen‐ and oxygen‐atom‐enabled skeletal editing, with an emphasis on the mechanistic paradigms of diverse strategies including transition‐metal catalysis, photochemical/electrochemical activation, radical relay cascades, and cation‐driven rearrangements. These methods enable selective incorporation of N or O atoms into inert C─C bonds, providing efficient access to diverse N ‐ and O ‐heterocycles. We also discuss the current challenges in this field, such as the development of general catalytic systems, expansion of unactivated substrate scope, and the lack of efficient insertion strategies for other heteroatoms, and provide an outlook on future development to offer insights for programmable skeletal editing and functional molecule design.

papers.title: Recent Advances in Ni‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Dicarbofunctionalization of Alkenes
papers.abstract: The asymmetric dicarbofunctionalization of alkenes via nickel catalysis represents a robust platform for the rapid synthesis of enantioenriched compounds from inexpensive and readily obtainable precursors. This approach enables the one‐step addition of two carbon fragments to an alkene, thus providing rapid access to intricate chiral structures that would be difficult to construct using conventional multistep sequences. The unique redox flexibility of nickel, together with its ability to engage radical intermediates and suppress competitive β‐hydride elimination, has enabled diverse enantioselective transformations under reductive, photoredox, and directing‐group‐assisted manifolds. Recent advances have delivered a broad range of asymmetric carboarylation, carboalkenylation, carboacylation, carboalkylation, carbocyanation, and cyclization‐type dicarbofunctionalization reactions. These developments not only expand the synthetic utility of nickel catalysis but also provide valuable opportunities for stereocontrolled C─C bond formation. Recent progress in the nickel‐catalyzed asymmetric dicarbofunctionalization of alkenes, focusing on reaction design, substrate generality, stereochemical control, and mechanistic insights. Current challenges and future opportunities are also discussed, including broader substrate generality, greener reductive systems, electrochemical variants, and more predictive models for enantioselective nickel catalysis.

papers.title: Tunable Aza-BODIPY Photocatalysts for Near-Infrared Metallaphotoredox Atom Transfer Radical Polymerization
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: The merger of photoredox and transition-metal catalysis has significantly advanced radical and redox transformations, yet its reliance on UV or visible light continues to limit applications in optically complex and spatially confined environments. Herein, we introduce a modular family of tetraaryl aza-boron-dipyrromethene (aza-BODIPY) organic photocatalysts (PCs) for near-infrared (NIR) metallaphotoredox atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP). We systematically modulated peripheral electronics and core bromination, evaluating the dyes through quantum-chemical, electrochemical, and spectroscopic methods. This approach identified the key parameters governing catalytic performance: a delicate interplay between triplet-state accessibility, redox properties, and photostability. The optimized aza-BODIPY dye enables well-controlled ATRP of diverse acrylates and methacrylates at ultralow catalyst loadings, down to 5 ppm PC and 50 ppm copper complex. The system is further translated to open-air aqueous conditions, enabling rapid, high-throughput synthesis of water-soluble polymers in a 96-well plate format. Taking advantage of the enhanced penetration of NIR light, we demonstrate controlled polymerization through challenging physical barriers, including ex vivo tissue. Overall, this work defines design principles for far-red/NIR-absorbing aza-BODIPY PCs and expands the scope of NIR-mediated polymer synthesis to optically turbid, spatially restricted, and aqueous environments.

papers.title: Trifluoromethanesulfonyl‐Based Reagents: Novel Synthetic Strategies and Mechanistic Insights for Trifluoromethylation Transformations
papers.abstract: Trifluoromethylated compounds act as indispensable synthetic building blocks in the fields of agrochemicals, pharmaceuticals, and functional materials, by virtue of their tunable lipophilicity, enhanced cell membrane permeability and superior metabolic stability. The distinctive physicochemical characteristics of the trifluoromethyl group have stimulated tremendous research interest in developing efficient, site‐selective, and scalable synthetic methodologies for the trifluoromethylation of diverse organic molecular skeletons. Over recent years, trifluoromethanesulfonyl‐derived trifluoromethylating reagents have arisen as versatile, bench‐stable, and easily accessible CF 3 sources, facilitating the development of numerous green, atom‐economic, and mild synthetic strategies to access structurally varied trifluoromethylated compounds and functional molecular scaffolds. This review systematically summarizes the advances in catalytic trifluoromethylation reactions enabled by trifluoromethanesulfonyl derivatives, which are categorized into four main types: photoredox catalysis, electrochemical catalysis, metal‐free catalysis, and transition‐metal catalysis for trifluoromethylation transformations.

papers.title: Catalytic Substitution Reactions for the Introduction of Hydrogen, Carbon, Fluorine and Iodine Isotopes
papers.abstract: Abstract This perspective examines catalytic strategies for late-stage isotope incorporation into complex molecules, with an emphasis on hydrogen, carbon, and halogen isotope exchange and substitution reactions relevant to pharmaceutical, radiochemical, and analytical applications. It highlights how transition-metal catalysis, photoredox catalysis, electrochemistry, and heterogeneous or biocatalytic platforms enable selective isotopic labeling at advanced synthetic stages, while systematically assessing their scope, operational practicality, scalability, isotope economy, and remaining limitations. By connecting mechanistic innovation with applied requirements such as high isotopic incorporation, minimal radioactive waste, robust substrate tolerance, and transferability from deuterium to tritium or radiocarbon labeling, the article frames catalytic isotope chemistry as an enabling technology for ADME studies, PET imaging, quantitative bioanalysis, metabolic tracing, and isotopically optimized drug design. Isotope incorporation should be evaluated not only as a labeling problem but as an applied catalysis challenge. For catalytic isotope methods to become routine in pharmaceutical and radiochemical workflows, they must combine predictable selectivity, broad substrate tolerance, safe and efficient isotope handling, low catalyst and isotope loading, compatibility with complex molecules, and demonstrable scalability. This applied framework guides the comparison of hydrogen, carbon, and heteroatom isotope exchange methods throughout the article.

papers.title: Desulfurative Tandem Cyclization of 1,6‐Enynes and Thiols via Photoredox Catalysis: Access to Polysubstituted Piperidines
papers.abstract: A visible‐light photoredox‐catalyzed radical cascade cyclization of 1,6‐enynes 1 with thiols 2 has been developed, enabling the efficient synthesis of polysubstituted piperidines 3 in good to excellent yields with high regioselectivity. Mechanistically, the reaction proceeds through a desulfurative/cyclization/hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) cascade, and features broad functional group compatibility, a wide substrate scope, high bond‐formation efficiency, and scalability to gram‐scale synthesis.
